sw.R: Abimeleki alikuwa mmoja wa wana wa Yerubaali, yule aliyeitwa pia Gideoni. Abimeleki alikwenda Shekemu, walikoishi jamaa za mama yake. Alizungumza nao na watu wote wa ukoo wa jamaa ya mama yake. Akasema,

es.B: Abimelec hijo de Jerobaal fue a Siquem, a los parientes de su madre, y les habló a ellos y a todo el clan de la familia de su madre. Les dijo:
es.R: Abimelec era hijo de Jerobaal, el hombre a quien también llamaban Gedeón. Abimelec fue a Siquem, donde vivían los parientes de su madre. Les habló a ellos y a todo el clan de la familia de su madre. Les dijo:

decisions.choice: Abimelech son of Jerubbaal: Gideon's son by his concubine from Shechem
decisions.reason: Jerubbaal is Gideon's other name (6:32; 7:1). Gideon had seventy sons by his many wives (8:30), and Abimelech was the son of his concubine who lived in Shechem (8:31). That is why Abimelech turns to his mother's family there: through her he belongs to Shechem, while his half-brothers belong to Ophrah.

decisions.choice: his mother's brothers: his relatives on his mother's side
decisions.reason: The word "brothers" often means kinsmen in general (Genesis 13:8; 29:15). The next words widen the circle to the whole clan of his mother's father, so the men meant are her family, not only her own brothers.

decisions.choice: Abimelech: the name means "my father is king"
decisions.reason: Gideon refused to rule over Israel and said that neither he nor his son would rule; the LORD would rule (8:22-23). Yet he gave this son a name that means "my father is king" (8:31). The chapter tells how the son tried to make the name come true.

decisions.choice: relatives / his mother's family
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "relatives" and "family" for "brothers" and "house of the father", since the Hebrew means the wider kin (m2). Literal keeps "brothers".

decisions.choice: the man also called Gideon
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader that Jerubbaal is Gideon, the hero of chapters 6-8, which the Hebrew assumes the reader knows (6:32).

source.text: דַּבְּרוּ־נָ֞א בְּאָזְנֵ֨י כָל־בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶם֮ מַה־טּ֣וֹב לָכֶם֒ הַמְשֹׁ֨ל בָּכֶ֜ם שִׁבְעִ֣ים אִ֗ישׁ כֹּ֚ל בְּנֵ֣י יְרֻבַּ֔עַל אִם־מְשֹׁ֥ל בָּכֶ֖ם אִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֑ד וּזְכַרְתֶּ֕ם כִּֽי־עַצְמֵכֶםוּבְשַׂרְכֶ֖ם אָנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Speak, please, in [the] ears of all [the] lords of Shechem: what [is] good for you, to rule over you seventy men, all [the] sons of Jerubbaal, or to rule over you one man? And remember that your bone and your flesh I [am].

en.L: "Speak, please, in the ears of all the lords of Shechem: 'Which [is] better for you, that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or that one man rule over you? And remember that I [am] your bone and your flesh.'"
en.B: "Please put this question to all the leaders of Shechem: 'Which is better for you, to be ruled by seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, or to be ruled by one man? Remember that I am your own flesh and blood.'"
en.R: "Ask all the leaders of Shechem this: 'Would you rather have all seventy of Jerubbaal's sons ruling over you, or just one man? Remember, I am your own relative.'"

sw.L: "Semeni, tafadhali, masikioni mwa wakuu wote wa Shekemu: 'Ni lipi [lililo] bora kwenu, watu sabini, wana wote wa Yerubaali, watawale juu yenu, au mtu mmoja atawale juu yenu? Nanyi kumbukeni kwamba mimi [ni] mfupa wenu na nyama yenu.'"
sw.B: "Tafadhali waulizeni viongozi wote wa Shekemu swali hili: 'Ni lipi lililo bora kwenu, kutawaliwa na watu sabini, wana wote wa Yerubaali, au kutawaliwa na mtu mmoja? Kumbukeni kwamba mimi ni damu yenu na nyama yenu.'"
sw.R: "Waulizeni viongozi wote wa Shekemu hivi: 'Mnapenda zaidi wana wote sabini wa Yerubaali watawale juu yenu, au mtu mmoja tu? Kumbukeni, mimi ni ndugu yenu.'"

es.L: «{{plural_you:Hablen|Hablad}}, por favor, a oídos de todos los señores de Siquem: “¿Qué [es] mejor para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que setenta hombres, todos los hijos de Jerobaal, gobiernen sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, o que gobierne sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} un solo hombre? {{plural_you:Recuerden|Recordad}} también que yo [soy] {{plural_you:su hueso y su carne|vuestro hueso y vuestra carne}}.”»
es.B: «Por favor, {{plural_you:pregúntenles|preguntadles}} esto a todos los líderes de Siquem: “¿Qué es mejor para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que {{plural_you:los gobiernen|os gobiernen}} setenta hombres, todos los hijos de Jerobaal, o que {{plural_you:los gobierne|os gobierne}} un solo hombre? {{plural_you:Recuerden|Recordad}} que yo soy de {{plural_you:su propia sangre|vuestra propia sangre}}.”»
es.R: «{{plural_you:Pregúntenles|Preguntadles}} esto a todos los líderes de Siquem: “¿Qué {{plural_you:prefieren|preferís}}, que los setenta hijos de Jerobaal {{plural_you:los gobiernen|os gobiernen}}, o que {{plural_you:los gobierne|os gobierne}} un solo hombre? {{plural_you:Recuerden|Recordad}} que yo soy pariente {{plural_you:suyo|vuestro}}.”»

decisions.choice: the lords of Shechem: the leading landholders who governed the city
decisions.reason: The word ba'al means owner or master, and "the ba'als of a city" are its free landowning men, the body that could make decisions for the city, make a king (verse 6) and break with him (verse 23). The phrase comes back sixteen times in this chapter. It is the same word as the name of the god Baal, whose temple they serve (verse 4), so the story plays on who is truly lord in Shechem.

decisions.choice: seventy ruling, or one: a choice Gideon had refused
decisions.reason: Gideon had said that neither he nor his sons would rule over Israel (8:22-23), and nothing says his sons ruled after him. Abimelech's question takes their rule for granted, to make one ruler look like the better choice.

decisions.choice: your bone and your flesh: your blood relative
decisions.reason: "Bone and flesh" is the language of close kinship (Genesis 2:23; 29:14; 2 Samuel 5:1). Abimelech's claim is that he is one of Shechem's own, unlike his brothers from Ophrah.

decisions.choice: lords (Literal); leaders (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "lords", which shows the root "owner, master" and its link with the god Baal. Balanced and Readable say "leaders", since "lords" suggests nobles or a feudal title to a modern reader. The same rendering is used through the chapter.

decisions.choice: your own flesh and blood / your own relative
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the English idiom for kinship, Readable the plain word; Literal keeps "bone and flesh".

decisions.choice: "wakuu wa Shekemu" (L) and "viongozi wa Shekemu" (B, R) for "the lords of Shechem", through the chapter
decisions.reason: The Hebrew calls the city's leading landholders by a word that also means "owners" or "masters". Literal says "wakuu" (chief men); Balanced and Readable say "viongozi" (leaders), as the English says "leaders".

decisions.choice: "los señores de Siquem" (L); "los líderes de Siquem" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word, the plural of "baal" ("owner, lord"), names the leading landholders who governed the city (m1). Literal keeps "señores", as the English keeps "lords"; Balanced and Readable say "líderes", as the English says "leaders".

source.text: וַיְדַבְּר֨וּ אֲחֵֽי־אִמּ֜וֹ עָלָ֗יו בְּאָזְנֵי֙ כָּל־בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֵּ֤ט לִבָּם֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ כִּ֥י אָמְר֖וּ אָחִ֥ינוּ הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke [the] brothers of his mother concerning him in [the] ears of all [the] lords of Shechem all these words, and inclined their heart after Abimelech, for they said, our brother [is] he.

en.L: And his mother's brothers spoke all these words about him in the ears of all the lords of Shechem, and their heart inclined after Abimelech, for they said, "He [is] our brother."
en.B: His mother's relatives spoke on his behalf and put all these words before the leaders of Shechem, and their hearts leaned toward Abimelech, because they said, "He is our own kin."
en.R: So his mother's relatives told all the leaders of Shechem what Abimelech had said. The leaders decided to follow Abimelech, because they said, "He is one of us."

sw.L: Nao ndugu za mama yake wakanena habari zake masikioni mwa wakuu wote wa Shekemu maneno haya yote, na moyo wao ukaelekea kumfuata Abimeleki, kwa maana walisema, "Yeye [ni] ndugu yetu."
sw.B: Jamaa za mama yake walimsemea, wakawaeleza viongozi wa Shekemu maneno hayo yote, na mioyo yao ikaelekea kwa Abimeleki, kwa sababu walisema, "Yeye ni ndugu yetu wa damu."
sw.R: Basi jamaa za mama yake waliwaambia viongozi wote wa Shekemu yale Abimeleki aliyosema. Viongozi waliamua kumfuata Abimeleki, kwa sababu walisema, "Yeye ni mmoja wetu."

es.L: Y los hermanos de su madre hablaron de él todas estas palabras a oídos de todos los señores de Siquem, y el corazón de ellos se inclinó tras Abimelec, porque dijeron: «Nuestro hermano [es] él.»
es.B: Los parientes de su madre hablaron en su favor y presentaron todas estas palabras a los líderes de Siquem, y el corazón de ellos se inclinó hacia Abimelec, porque dijeron: «Es de nuestra propia sangre.»
es.R: Así que los parientes de su madre les contaron a todos los líderes de Siquem lo que Abimelec había dicho. Los líderes decidieron seguir a Abimelec, porque dijeron: «Es uno de los nuestros.»

decisions.choice: their heart inclined after Abimelech: they were won over to his side
decisions.reason: The heart is where a person decides. To have one's heart "incline after" someone is to lean toward him and choose to back him (1 Kings 11:3 uses the same picture for turning away).

decisions.choice: our brother: our own kin, one of us
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, "brother" means kinsman. The lords back him because his mother's family is from Shechem (8:31), not for anything he has done.

decisions.choice: He is one of us
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "our brother" (m2), since a young reader would take "brother" literally.

source.text: וַיִּתְּנוּ־לוֹ֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים כֶּ֔סֶף מִבֵּ֖יתּבַ֣עַלבְּרִ֑ית וַיִּשְׂכֹּ֨ר בָּהֶ֜ם אֲבִימֶ֗לֶךְ אֲנָשִׁ֤ים רֵיקִים֙ וּפֹ֣חֲזִ֔ים וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ אַחֲרָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And they gave to him seventy [pieces of] silver from [the] house of Baal-berith, and hired with them Abimelech men empty and reckless, and they went after him.

en.L: And they gave him seventy [pieces of] silver from the house of Baal-berith, and with it Abimelech hired empty and reckless men, and they followed him.
en.B: They gave him seventy pieces of silver from the temple of Baal-berith, and with that money Abimelech hired worthless, reckless men, who became his followers.
en.R: They gave him seventy pieces of silver from the temple of the god Baal-berith. Abimelech used the money to pay a gang of worthless troublemakers to follow him.

sw.L: Nao wakampa [vipande] sabini vya fedha kutoka nyumba ya Baal-berithi, naye Abimeleki akaajiri kwa fedha hiyo watu wasiofaa kitu na wakorofi, nao wakamfuata.
sw.B: Walimpa vipande sabini vya fedha kutoka hekalu la Baal-berithi, naye Abimeleki akatumia fedha hiyo kuajiri watu wasiofaa kitu na wakorofi, wakawa wafuasi wake.
sw.R: Walimpa vipande sabini vya fedha kutoka hekalu la mungu Baal-berithi. Abimeleki aliitumia fedha hiyo kuwalipa kundi la wahuni wasiofaa kitu ili wamfuate.

es.L: Y le dieron setenta [monedas de] plata de la casa de Baal-berit, y con ellas Abimelec contrató a hombres vacíos y temerarios, que lo siguieron.
es.B: Le dieron setenta piezas de plata del templo de Baal-berit, y con ese dinero Abimelec contrató a hombres sin valor y temerarios, que se hicieron sus seguidores.
es.R: Le dieron setenta piezas de plata del templo del dios Baal-berit. Abimelec usó el dinero para pagarle a una banda de alborotadores sin valor para que lo siguieran.

decisions.choice: the house of Baal-berith: the temple of "Baal of the covenant" in Shechem
decisions.reason: After Gideon died, Israel made Baal-berith its god (8:33). The name means "Baal of the covenant"; in verse 46 the god is called El-berith, "God of the covenant". Temples kept treasuries, so the money for Abimelech's plot came from the god's own store.

decisions.choice: seventy pieces of silver: one for each brother he would kill
decisions.reason: The weight is not named, though shekels are likely, which would make it a little under two pounds of silver. The number matches the seventy sons of Jerubbaal (verse 5): the price of the plot is one piece of silver a head.

decisions.choice: empty and reckless men: worthless men with nothing to lose, ready for anything
decisions.reason: "Empty" men are men of no worth or standing, the kind who gather round an outlaw (11:3; 2 Chronicles 13:7). "Reckless" describes people who act without restraint (Zephaniah 3:4). They are hired muscle, not an army.

decisions.choice: temple
decisions.reason: "House" of a god means its temple; Balanced and Readable say so. Literal keeps "house".

decisions.choice: the god Baal-berith
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the god" so that a new reader knows Baal-berith is a god, not a person.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֤א בֵית־אָבִיו֙ עָפְרָ֔תָה וַֽיַּהֲרֹ֞ג אֶת־אֶחָ֧יו בְּנֵֽי־יְרֻבַּ֛עַל שִׁבְּעִ֥יםאִ֖ישׁ עַל־אֶ֣בֶן אֶחָ֑ת וַיִּוָּתֵ֞ר יוֹתָ֧ם בֶּן־יְרֻבַּ֛עַל הַקָּטֹ֖ן כִּ֥י נֶחְבָּֽא׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he went [to the] house of his father at Ophrah, and killed his brothers, [the] sons of Jerubbaal, seventy men, on one stone; and was left Jotham, son of Jerubbaal, the youngest, for he hid himself.

en.L: And he went to his father's house at Ophrah and killed his brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal, seventy men, on one stone. But Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, was left, for he hid himself.
en.B: He went to his father's home at Ophrah and killed his brothers, the seventy sons of Jerubbaal, on a single stone. But Jotham, Jerubbaal's youngest son, survived because he had gone into hiding.
en.R: He went to his father's home in the town of Ophrah. There, on one stone, he killed his brothers, the seventy sons of Jerubbaal. Only Jotham, the youngest son, was left alive, because he hid.

sw.L: Naye akaenda nyumbani kwa baba yake huko Ofra, akawaua ndugu zake, wana wa Yerubaali, watu sabini, juu ya jiwe moja. Lakini Yothamu, mwana mdogo wa Yerubaali, akabaki, kwa maana alijificha.
sw.B: Alikwenda nyumbani kwa baba yake huko Ofra, akawaua ndugu zake, wana sabini wa Yerubaali, juu ya jiwe moja. Lakini Yothamu, mwana mdogo kabisa wa Yerubaali, aliokoka kwa sababu alikuwa amejificha.
sw.R: Alikwenda nyumbani kwa baba yake katika mji wa Ofra. Huko, juu ya jiwe moja, aliwaua ndugu zake, wana sabini wa Yerubaali. Ni Yothamu tu, mwana mdogo kabisa, aliyebaki hai, kwa sababu alijificha.

es.L: Y fue a la casa de su padre en Ofra, y mató a sus hermanos, los hijos de Jerobaal, setenta hombres, sobre una misma piedra; pero quedó Jotam, el hijo menor de Jerobaal, porque se escondió.
es.B: Fue a la casa de su padre en Ofra y mató a sus hermanos, los setenta hijos de Jerobaal, sobre una sola piedra. Pero Jotam, el hijo menor de Jerobaal, sobrevivió porque se había escondido.
es.R: Fue a la casa de su padre en la ciudad de Ofra. Allí, sobre una sola piedra, mató a sus hermanos, los setenta hijos de Jerobaal. Solo Jotam, el hijo menor, quedó con vida, porque se escondió.

decisions.choice: on one stone: killed one after another in one place, like a slaughter
decisions.reason: Killing them all on one stone makes the murder a single, deliberate execution. A stone was where animals were slaughtered (1 Samuel 14:33-34), so the phrase may also make the deed look like a sacrifice. Jotham repeats the words in verse 18, and the chapter ends with a stone falling on Abimelech's head (verse 53).

decisions.choice: seventy men: the whole number of Gideon's sons, given in round figures
decisions.reason: Gideon had seventy sons (8:30), and Jotham, one of them, escapes. So either "seventy" is the round number for all of them, or Gideon's sons with Abimelech made seventy-one. Either way the point is that the whole family was wiped out but one.

decisions.choice: the town of Ophrah
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the town of" so that a new reader knows Ophrah is a place (6:11).

source.text: וַיֵּאָ֨סְפ֜וּ כָּל־בַּעֲלֵ֤י שְׁכֶם֙ וְכָל־בֵּ֣ית מִלּ֔וֹא וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ וַיַּמְלִ֥יכוּ אֶת־אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ לְמֶ֑לֶךְ עִם־אֵל֥וֹן מֻצָּ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּשְׁכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And gathered all [the] lords of Shechem and all Beth-millo, and they went and made king Abimelech as king by [the] oak of [the] pillar that [is] in Shechem.

en.L: And all the lords of Shechem and all Beth-millo gathered, and they went and made Abimelech king by the oak of the pillar that [is] in Shechem.
en.B: Then all the leaders of Shechem and all of Beth-millo came together and went and made Abimelech king beside the oak of the standing stone at Shechem.
en.R: Then all the leaders of Shechem and everyone from Beth-millo met together. They made Abimelech their king beside the oak tree near the standing stone in Shechem.

sw.L: Nao wakuu wote wa Shekemu na Beth-milo yote wakakusanyika, wakaenda wakamtawaza Abimeleki kuwa mfalme karibu na mwaloni wa nguzo [ulio] Shekemu.
sw.B: Kisha viongozi wote wa Shekemu na watu wote wa Beth-milo walikusanyika, wakaenda wakamtawaza Abimeleki kuwa mfalme karibu na mwaloni wa jiwe la kusimamishwa huko Shekemu.
sw.R: Kisha viongozi wote wa Shekemu na watu wote wa Beth-milo walikutana pamoja. Walimfanya Abimeleki kuwa mfalme wao karibu na mti wa mwaloni ulio karibu na jiwe lililosimamishwa huko Shekemu.

es.L: Y se reunieron todos los señores de Siquem y toda Bet-milo, y fueron y proclamaron rey a Abimelec junto a la encina del pilar que [está] en Siquem.
es.B: Entonces todos los líderes de Siquem y todo Bet-milo se reunieron y fueron y proclamaron rey a Abimelec junto a la encina de la piedra levantada que hay en Siquem.
es.R: Entonces todos los líderes de Siquem y toda la gente de Bet-milo se reunieron. Hicieron rey a Abimelec junto a la encina que está cerca de la piedra levantada en Siquem.

decisions.choice: Beth-millo: a fortified part of Shechem, or the people who held it
decisions.reason: The name means "house of the filling", probably a fort built on a raised platform of packed earth (compare "the Millo" in Jerusalem, 2 Samuel 5:9). It may be the same place as the Tower of Shechem (verses 46-49). Its exact site is not known.

decisions.choice: the oak of the pillar at Shechem: the place where Israel had sworn to serve the LORD
decisions.reason: At Shechem Joshua set up a great stone under the oak by the sanctuary as a witness to Israel's covenant with the LORD (Joshua 24:25-27). Jacob had buried foreign gods under the oak at Shechem (Genesis 35:4). Abimelech is made king at the very spot where Israel had promised to serve God alone.

decisions.choice: the standing stone
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means something set up, here a stone pillar (m2). Balanced and Readable say "standing stone" so that it is not taken for a building's column; Literal keeps "pillar".

source.text: וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ לְיוֹתָ֗ם וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הַר־גְּרִזִ֔ים וַיִּשָּׂ֥א קוֹל֖וֹ וַיִּקְרָ֑א וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם וְיִשְׁמַ֥ע אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they told Jotham, and he went and stood on [the] top of Mount Gerizim, and lifted his voice and called, and said to them, listen to me, lords of Shechem, and may listen to you God.

en.L: And they told Jotham, and he went and stood on the top of Mount Gerizim, and he lifted up his voice and called out and said to them, "Listen to me, lords of Shechem, so that God may listen to you.

decisions.choice: Mount Gerizim: the mountain of blessing that rises over Shechem
decisions.reason: Gerizim stands just above the city. Moses ordered that the blessings of the covenant be spoken from Gerizim and the curses from Ebal (Deuteronomy 11:29; 27:12), and Joshua did so (Joshua 8:33). From the mountain of blessing Jotham speaks what turns into a curse (verse 57).

decisions.choice: listen to me, so that God may listen to you: hearing Jotham is the condition of God's hearing them
decisions.reason: The second verb depends on the first: if the lords will listen to Jotham's case, God will listen to them. It warns them that their standing before God depends on how they answer for what was done to Jerubbaal's house.

decisions.choice: if you want God to listen to you
decisions.reason: Readable makes the link between the two clauses plain (m2).

decisions.choice: the trees went out: a fable, a story in which plants speak
decisions.reason: Jotham tells a fable, a short tale with talking plants that teaches a lesson, like the one King Jehoash tells in 2 Kings 14:9. The doubled verb ("going they went") opens the tale with weight, much like "once upon a time". The trees stand for the lords of Shechem, and each plant for a kind of ruler.

decisions.choice: to anoint a king: to make a king by pouring oil on him
decisions.reason: Kings in Israel were made by anointing with olive oil (1 Samuel 10:1; 16:13). The trees go first to the olive, the very tree that gives the oil of anointing.

decisions.choice: Be our king
decisions.reason: "Reign over us" is said more naturally in present-day English as "Be our king"; Literal keeps "Reign over us". The same wording returns in verses 10, 12 and 14.

decisions.choice: verses 8-15 set in poetic lines
decisions.reason: The fable is set in lines, as the Hebrew accents divide it, at every level.

decisions.choice: Readable opens the fable with "Hapo zamani za kale" (once upon a time); the fable is set in lines at every level, as in the English
decisions.reason: "Hapo zamani za kale" is how a Swahili tale begins, as "once upon a time" is in English, and it tells the reader at once that Jotham is telling a fable in which trees speak.

decisions.choice: the fable (verses 8-15) set in lines, as the English sets it; the trees' words in “ ” inside Jotham's «»
decisions.reason: As the terms note for these books sets, Jotham's fable is set in lines at the levels where the English has them, with the breaks at Spanish phrase boundaries. The trees speak to one tree at a time ("Reina", "Sé nuestro rey", with "tú"), and the bramble answers all the trees in the plural.

decisions.choice: my fatness: my rich oil
decisions.reason: The word means fatness or richness, here the olive's oil, the best thing it gives. Oil was used to anoint priests and kings, to honor guests, and in offerings (Leviticus 2:1; Psalm 23:5).

decisions.choice: God and men: God and human beings, all who are honored with oil
decisions.reason: The word elohim can mean God or gods. In Israel, oil and wine (verse 13) are offered to God (Leviticus 2:1; Numbers 15:5-10), and Jotham has just called on God (verse 7), so God is meant. But in a fable the pair can also be a fixed phrase, "gods and men", for everyone above and below.

decisions.choice: go to sway over the trees: give up a useful life for an empty, restless rule
decisions.reason: The verb means to wave, sway or wander (Isaiah 7:2; Psalm 109:10). Ruling is pictured as swaying back and forth above the others, with nothing produced. The good trees refuse to trade their fruitfulness for it.

decisions.choice: people / humans
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general, as the pair "God and men" shows. Balanced and Readable use inclusive words, and the reader's gender setting can show "men".

decisions.choice: just to
decisions.reason: Readable adds "just" to bring out the scorn of the question: the trade would be a poor one.

decisions.choice: the bramble: a low thorny shrub, good for nothing but burning
decisions.reason: The word names a thorny bush, probably the buckthorn of the hills of Israel (Psalm 58:10). It gives no fruit, no oil and almost no shade, and its dry wood catches fire quickly. This time "all the trees" ask, the whole city turning to the least worthy plant of all.

decisions.choice: thornbush
decisions.reason: Readable says "thornbush", a commoner word than "bramble"; it names the same plant. Readable also adds "At last", since this is the last plant the trees ask.

decisions.choice: "mchongoma" (L, B) and "kichaka cha miiba" (R) for the bramble
decisions.reason: "Mchongoma" is a low thorny shrub, good for hedges and for burning, which is the picture: a plant that gives no shade worth having. Readable says plainly "a thornbush", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: take refuge in my shade: trust me for protection, a promise the bramble cannot keep
decisions.reason: "Shade" is the protection a king gives his people (Isaiah 30:2-3; Lamentations 4:20). A low thornbush can give no shade to a tree; the offer is empty and the picture absurd. The bramble asks the great trees to bow down beneath it.

decisions.choice: in truth: in good faith, honestly meant
decisions.reason: The bramble asks whether the trees mean it. Jotham takes up the same words in verses 16 and 19: did the lords act "in truth" when they made Abimelech king?

decisions.choice: fire from the bramble devouring the cedars of Lebanon: the worthless ruler destroys the greatest
decisions.reason: Dry thornbushes catch fire easily and spread it to everything around them (Exodus 22:5; Isaiah 9:17). The cedars of Lebanon were the tallest and finest trees known in Israel. Jotham applies the threat in verse 20, and it comes true in verses 49 and 57.

decisions.choice: even the great cedar trees
decisions.reason: Readable adds "great" and "even" to show why the cedars are named: the fire of the smallest plant reaches the mightiest trees.

decisions.choice: a broken sentence: the condition begun here is taken up again in verse 19
decisions.reason: Jotham starts a long "if ...", breaks off in verses 17-18 to remind them what Gideon did and what they have done, and then starts again in verse 19 with "if, then". The interruption is part of the speech's force.

decisions.choice: in truth and in integrity: the words of the covenant made at Shechem
decisions.reason: At Shechem Joshua told Israel to serve the LORD "in integrity and in truth" (Joshua 24:14). Jotham asks the lords of Shechem whether they have kept faith in that way with the family of the man who saved them.

decisions.choice: according to the deed of his hands: as his actions deserved
decisions.reason: "The dealing of his hands" means what a man has done for others. To do to him "according to" it is to repay him fairly for it (Proverbs 12:14; Isaiah 3:11).

decisions.choice: questions in place of the conditions
decisions.reason: Readable turns Jotham's long "if" clauses into questions, so the reader is not left waiting through verses 17-18 for the end of the sentence.

decisions.choice: threw his life away in front of him: risked his life
decisions.reason: To "throw one's life away" is to put it in danger without holding anything back, as Jephthah says he "put his life in his hand" (12:3).

decisions.choice: delivered you from the hand of Midian: Gideon's victory in chapters 6-8
decisions.reason: For seven years Midian had stripped the land (6:1-6), until God saved Israel through Gideon (7:22; 8:28). The lords of Shechem owed their freedom to the man whose sons they have just killed.

decisions.choice: Remember
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence with "Remember" for the interruption that the Hebrew joins with "for" (see verse 16).

decisions.choice: the son of his slave woman: a mother of low, unfree standing
decisions.reason: The word amah means a female slave. In 8:31 she is called Gideon's concubine, a secondary wife. Jotham uses the lowest word he can to shame Abimelech and those who chose him: they have killed the sons of a free house for the son of a slave.

decisions.choice: you have killed his sons: you share the guilt, though Abimelech struck the blows
decisions.reason: The lords did not kill the brothers with their own hands, but they paid for it (verse 4). Jotham charges them with the murder, as the narrator does in verse 24.

decisions.choice: he is your brother: he is your kinsman
decisions.reason: Jotham throws their own words back at them (verse 3). Abimelech was also the brother of the seventy he killed.

decisions.choice: slave woman
decisions.reason: "Slave" is kept at every level, because her unfree status is the point of Jotham's insult; "servant" would lose it (see the style guide on 'eved).

decisions.choice: the insult moved to the end
decisions.reason: Readable puts the insult in a sentence of its own at the end, where it keeps its force without crowding the list of charges.

decisions.choice: "mjakazi" (slave woman) for Abimelech's mother at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word names a woman of unfree standing, and Jotham uses it as an insult. "Mjakazi" is the Swahili word for a female slave or bondwoman and carries that low standing; the English keeps "slave woman" at every level too.

decisions.choice: fire from Abimelech: the bramble's fire of verse 15 applied
decisions.reason: Abimelech is the bramble, and the lords of Shechem are the trees that chose him. Each side will destroy the other. The curse comes true when Abimelech burns the Tower of Shechem (verse 49) and is himself killed (verses 53-54); verse 57 calls it "the curse of Jotham".

decisions.choice: a curse laid before God
decisions.reason: Jotham has asked God to listen (verse 7). His words are not a magic spell but an appeal for God to judge between the two sides, and the narrator says that God did so (verses 23-24, 56-57).

en.R: Then Jotham ran away. He went to the town of Beer and lived there, because he was afraid of his brother Abimelech.

decisions.choice: Beer: a town whose site is unknown
decisions.reason: The name means "well", and several places in Israel bore it (Numbers 21:16). Which one Jotham fled to is not known; it was far enough from Abimelech to be safe.

decisions.choice: from before Abimelech: to escape him, for fear of him
decisions.reason: "From before" someone means out of his presence, often in fear (1 Samuel 21:11). Jotham is safe only where Abimelech cannot reach him.

decisions.choice: because he was afraid of
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly why Jotham stayed away (m2), and adds "the town of" before Beer.

records.literal_gloss: And ruled Abimelech over Israel three years.

en.L: And Abimelech ruled over Israel three years.
en.B: Abimelech held power over Israel for three years.
en.R: Abimelech ruled over Israel for three years.

sw.L: Naye Abimeleki akatawala juu ya Israeli miaka mitatu.
sw.B: Abimeleki aliwatawala Israeli kwa miaka mitatu.
sw.R: Abimeleki alitawala juu ya Israeli kwa miaka mitatu.

es.L: Y Abimelec dominó sobre Israel tres años.
es.B: Abimelec tuvo el poder sobre Israel durante tres años.
es.R: Abimelec gobernó sobre Israel durante tres años.

decisions.choice: ruled: held power, not "reigned as king"
decisions.reason: The verb here is not the one for reigning as king that the chapter has used (verses 6, 8-14), nor "judged" (2:16). It means to act as a prince or commander. The narrator holds back the title the lords of Shechem gave him.

decisions.choice: over Israel: over the part of Israel he controlled
decisions.reason: Abimelech's power seems to reach no further than Shechem and the towns near it (verses 41, 50), but those who fought for him are called "the men of Israel" (verse 55). "Israel" here is the Israelite people he held under him, not necessarily all the tribes.

en.L: And God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the lords of Shechem, and the lords of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech,
en.B: Then God sent an evil spirit to come between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem broke faith with Abimelech,
en.R: Then God sent an evil spirit that turned Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem against each other. The leaders of Shechem turned traitor against Abimelech.

sw.L: Naye Mungu akatuma roho mbaya kati ya Abimeleki na wakuu wa Shekemu, nao wakuu wa Shekemu wakamtendea Abimeleki kwa hila,
sw.B: Kisha Mungu alituma roho mbaya ije kati ya Abimeleki na viongozi wa Shekemu, nao viongozi wa Shekemu wakavunja uaminifu wao kwa Abimeleki,
sw.R: Kisha Mungu alituma roho mbaya iliyowagombanisha Abimeleki na viongozi wa Shekemu. Viongozi wa Shekemu wakamsaliti Abimeleki.

es.L: Y envió Dios un espíritu malo entre Abimelec y los señores de Siquem, y los señores de Siquem actuaron traicioneramente con Abimelec,
es.B: Entonces Dios envió un espíritu malo que se interpuso entre Abimelec y los líderes de Siquem, y los líderes de Siquem le fueron desleales a Abimelec,
es.R: Entonces Dios envió un espíritu malo que puso a Abimelec y a los líderes de Siquem el uno contra el otro. Los líderes de Siquem traicionaron a Abimelec.

decisions.choice: an evil spirit: a spirit that brings harm and strife
decisions.reason: The word ra'ah can mean moral evil, but also harm, trouble or disaster (Amos 3:6; Isaiah 45:7). Here the spirit does its work "between" two allies, so it brings ill will and division. The same phrase is used of the spirit that troubled Saul (1 Samuel 16:14-16; 18:10). Whether a spirit-being is meant or a temper of hostility sent among them, the Hebrew does not say.

decisions.choice: God sent it: God acts in judgment through the people's own falseness
decisions.reason: The narrator gives the reason at once (verse 24): the murder of the seventy must be repaid. God does not make the lords sin; they had already acted without good faith (verses 16-19). God turns the alliance they built on murder against itself, as Jotham had asked (verses 7, 20). Scripture speaks the same way of God sending a deceiving spirit to judge King Ahab (1 Kings 22:19-23). God remains the judge who pays back evil (verses 56-57), not its author.

decisions.choice: dealt treacherously: broke faith, betrayed
decisions.reason: The verb is used of breaking a covenant or a marriage (Malachi 2:14; Jeremiah 3:20). The men who chose Abimelech "in truth" (verses 16, 19) now betray him in turn.

decisions.choice: that turned ... against each other
decisions.reason: Readable says what the spirit did "between" them, as the second half of the verse shows (m1).

decisions.choice: broke faith with
decisions.reason: Balanced says "broke faith with" for the verb of betrayal; Literal keeps "dealt treacherously".

source.text: לָב֕וֹא חֲמַ֖ס שִׁבְעִ֣ים בְּנֵֽי־יְרֻבָּ֑עַל וְדָמָ֗ם לָשׂ֞וּם עַל־אֲבִימֶ֤לֶךְ אֲחִיהֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָרַ֣ג אוֹתָ֔ם וְעַל֙ בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־חִזְּק֥וּ אֶת־יָדָ֖יו לַהֲרֹ֥ג אֶת־אֶחָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: to come [the] violence [done to the] seventy sons of Jerubbaal, and their blood to put on Abimelech their brother, who killed them, and on [the] lords of Shechem, who strengthened his hands to kill his brothers.

en.L: so that the violence [done to] the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come, and their blood be laid on Abimelech their brother, who killed them, and on the lords of Shechem, who strengthened his hands to kill his brothers.
en.B: so that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal would come back on those who did it, and the guilt for their blood would fall on their brother Abimelech, who killed them, and on the leaders of Shechem, who helped him kill his brothers.
en.R: God did this so that Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem would be punished for the murder of Jerubbaal's seventy sons. Abimelech had killed his own brothers, and the leaders of Shechem had helped him do it.

sw.L: ili jeuri [waliyotendewa] wana sabini wa Yerubaali ije, na damu yao iwekwe juu ya Abimeleki ndugu yao, aliyewaua, na juu ya wakuu wa Shekemu, walioitia nguvu mikono yake kuwaua ndugu zake.
sw.B: ili jeuri waliyotendewa wana sabini wa Yerubaali iwarudie waliyoitenda, na hatia ya damu yao imwangukie Abimeleki ndugu yao, aliyewaua, na viongozi wa Shekemu, waliomsaidia kuwaua ndugu zake.
sw.R: Mungu alifanya hivyo ili Abimeleki na viongozi wa Shekemu waadhibiwe kwa mauaji ya wana sabini wa Yerubaali. Abimeleki alikuwa amewaua ndugu zake mwenyewe, na viongozi wa Shekemu walikuwa wamemsaidia kufanya hivyo.

es.L: para que la violencia [hecha a] los setenta hijos de Jerobaal viniera, y su sangre recayera sobre Abimelec su hermano, que los mató, y sobre los señores de Siquem, que fortalecieron sus manos para matar a sus hermanos.
es.B: para que la violencia hecha a los setenta hijos de Jerobaal recayera sobre los que la cometieron, y la culpa de su sangre cayera sobre su hermano Abimelec, que los mató, y sobre los líderes de Siquem, que lo ayudaron a matar a sus hermanos.
es.R: Dios hizo esto para que Abimelec y los líderes de Siquem fueran castigados por el asesinato de los setenta hijos de Jerobaal. Abimelec había matado a sus propios hermanos, y los líderes de Siquem lo habían ayudado a hacerlo.

decisions.choice: for the violence to come: for the crime to come back on those who did it
decisions.reason: Violence that "comes" is wrong that returns on the doer (Psalm 7:17). The verse names the purpose of what God did in verse 23.

decisions.choice: to put their blood on Abimelech: to make him bear the guilt of their murder
decisions.reason: Shed blood cries out for justice (Genesis 4:10; 9:6), and to have someone's blood "on" you is to carry the guilt for his death (Deuteronomy 19:10; 2 Samuel 1:16).

decisions.choice: who strengthened his hands: who backed him and made the murder possible
decisions.reason: To strengthen someone's hands is to give him the means and the courage to act (1 Samuel 23:16; Jeremiah 23:14). The lords gave Abimelech the silver to hire his men (verse 4).

decisions.choice: God did this
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and names God as the one acting, from verse 23.

decisions.choice: would come back on those who did it
decisions.reason: Balanced spells out what it means for the violence to "come" (m1); Literal keeps the bare verb.

source.text: וַיָּשִׂ֣ימוּ לוֹ֩ בַעֲלֵ֨י שְׁכֶ֜ם מְאָרְבִ֗ים עַ֚ל רָאשֵׁ֣י הֶהָרִ֔ים וַיִּגְזְל֗וּ אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲבֹ֥ר עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לַאֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And set for him [the] lords of Shechem ambushers on [the] tops of the mountains, and they robbed all who passed by them on the road. And it was told to Abimelech.

en.L: And the lords of Shechem set men lying in wait for him on the tops of the mountains, and they robbed everyone who passed by them on the road. And it was told to Abimelech.
en.B: The leaders of Shechem set men in ambush against him on the mountaintops, and they robbed everyone who came past them along the road. Abimelech was told about it.
en.R: The leaders of Shechem hid men on the hilltops to attack Abimelech. Those men robbed everyone who traveled along the road nearby. Someone told Abimelech what was happening.

sw.L: Nao wakuu wa Shekemu wakaweka watu wa kumvizia juu ya vilele vya milima, nao wakawanyang'anya wote waliopita karibu nao njiani. Naye Abimeleki akaambiwa.
sw.B: Viongozi wa Shekemu waliweka watu wa kumvizia juu ya vilele vya milima, nao wakawanyang'anya wote waliopita karibu nao njiani. Abimeleki akaambiwa habari hiyo.
sw.R: Viongozi wa Shekemu waliwaficha watu juu ya vilima ili wamshambulie Abimeleki. Watu hao waliwanyang'anya wote waliosafiri katika njia iliyokuwa karibu. Mtu fulani alimwambia Abimeleki yaliyokuwa yakitokea.

es.L: Y los señores de Siquem le pusieron emboscadas en las cumbres de los montes, y robaban a todos los que pasaban junto a ellos por el camino. Y se le avisó a Abimelec.
es.B: Los líderes de Siquem pusieron hombres emboscados contra él en las cumbres de los montes, y estos robaban a todos los que pasaban por el camino. Y se lo contaron a Abimelec.
es.R: Los líderes de Siquem escondieron hombres en lo alto de las colinas para atacar a Abimelec. Esos hombres robaban a todos los que pasaban por el camino cercano. Alguien le contó a Abimelec lo que estaba pasando.

decisions.choice: set ambushers for him: to waylay Abimelech, and to his harm
decisions.reason: "For him" can mean against him, lying in wait to catch him on the road, or to his harm, by robbing travelers he was meant to protect. The robbery shows that his rule could not keep the roads safe, and it may have cut off the tolls and trade he lived on.

decisions.choice: robbing travelers on the mountain roads
decisions.reason: Shechem lies in a pass between Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal, on a main road through the hill country. Bandits on the heights above it could stop all traffic through the pass.

decisions.choice: to attack Abimelech
decisions.reason: Readable takes "for him" as "against him", the first sense of m1, and keeps the robbery that follows.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֞א גַּ֤עַל בֶּן־עֶ֨בֶד֙ וְאֶחָ֔יו וַיַּעַבְר֖וּ בִּשְׁכֶ֑ם וַיִּבְטְחוּ־ב֖וֹ בַּעֲלֵ֥י שְׁכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers, and they passed over into Shechem, and trusted in him [the] lords of Shechem.

en.L: And Gaal son of Ebed came with his brothers, and they moved into Shechem, and the lords of Shechem put their trust in him.
en.B: Then Gaal son of Ebed arrived with his relatives and moved into Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem came to trust him.
en.R: Then a man named Gaal son of Ebed moved to Shechem with his relatives. The leaders of Shechem began to trust him.

sw.L: Naye Gaali mwana wa Ebedi akaja pamoja na ndugu zake, wakahamia Shekemu, nao wakuu wa Shekemu wakamwamini.
sw.B: Kisha Gaali mwana wa Ebedi alifika pamoja na jamaa zake, akahamia Shekemu, nao viongozi wa Shekemu wakamwamini.
sw.R: Kisha mtu mmoja aitwaye Gaali mwana wa Ebedi alihamia Shekemu pamoja na jamaa zake. Viongozi wa Shekemu wakaanza kumwamini.

es.L: Y vino Gaal hijo de Ebed con sus hermanos, y pasaron a Siquem, y los señores de Siquem pusieron su confianza en él.
es.B: Entonces llegó Gaal hijo de Ebed con sus parientes y se mudó a Siquem, y los líderes de Siquem llegaron a confiar en él.
es.R: Entonces un hombre llamado Gaal hijo de Ebed se mudó a Siquem con sus parientes. Los líderes de Siquem empezaron a confiar en él.

decisions.choice: Gaal son of Ebed: a newcomer to Shechem
decisions.reason: Nothing is said of where Gaal came from. His father's name, Ebed, is the common word for "slave", and the story may enjoy the irony: the man who scorns serving Abimelech (verse 28) is "son of a slave", the charge Jotham made against Abimelech (verse 18).

decisions.choice: passed over into Shechem: came in and settled there
decisions.reason: The verb means to cross over or pass through; here it is the arrival of Gaal's clan in the city, where they stay (verse 41).

decisions.choice: relatives
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, "brothers" means kinsmen; Balanced and Readable say "relatives".

decisions.choice: "Gaal hijo de Ebed"; later "Zebul", "Hamor", "Aruma", "la Torre de Siquem", "El-berit", "el monte Salmón", "Tebes"
decisions.reason: Names in the usual Spanish forms; "Hamor" is the form of Genesis 34 in this translation, and "El-berit" matches "Baal-berit" of 8:33.

source.text: וַיֵּצְא֨וּ הַשָּׂדֶ֜ה וַֽיִּבְצְר֤וּ אֶת־כַּרְמֵיהֶם֙ וַֽיִּדְרְכ֔וּ וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֖וּ הִלּוּלִ֑ים וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית אֱֽלֹֽהֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּֽאכְלוּ֙ וַיִּשְׁתּ֔וּ וַֽיְקַלְל֖וּ אֶת־אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they went out [to] the field and gathered [the grapes of] their vineyards and trod [them] and made festival praises, and went into [the] house of their god and ate and drank and cursed Abimelech.

en.L: And they went out into the field and gathered [the grapes of] their vineyards and trod [them] and held a festival of praise, and they went into the house of their god and ate and drank and cursed Abimelech.
en.B: They went out to the fields, harvested the grapes from their vineyards and trod them, and held a harvest festival. They went into the temple of their god, ate and drank, and cursed Abimelech.
en.R: At harvest time they went out to their vineyards, picked the grapes, and crushed them to make wine. Then they held a festival. They went into the temple of their god, where they ate and drank and cursed Abimelech.

sw.L: Nao wakatoka [kwenda] shambani, wakachuma [zabibu za] mashamba yao ya mizabibu, wakazikanyaga, wakafanya sikukuu ya sifa, wakaingia katika nyumba ya mungu wao, wakala, wakanywa, wakamlaani Abimeleki.
sw.B: Walitoka kwenda mashambani, wakavuna zabibu za mashamba yao ya mizabibu, wakazikanyaga, wakafanya sikukuu ya mavuno. Wakaingia katika hekalu la mungu wao, wakala na kunywa, wakamlaani Abimeleki.
sw.R: Wakati wa mavuno walikwenda katika mashamba yao ya mizabibu, wakachuma zabibu na kuzikanyaga ili kutengeneza divai. Kisha wakafanya sikukuu. Waliingia katika hekalu la mungu wao, wakala na kunywa huko na kumlaani Abimeleki.

es.L: Y salieron al campo y vendimiaron sus viñas y [las] pisaron, e hicieron fiesta de alabanza, y entraron en la casa de su dios, y comieron y bebieron, y maldijeron a Abimelec.
es.B: Salieron a los campos, vendimiaron sus viñas, pisaron las uvas e hicieron una fiesta de la cosecha. Entraron en el templo de su dios, comieron y bebieron, y maldijeron a Abimelec.
es.R: En el tiempo de la cosecha salieron a sus viñas, cortaron las uvas y las pisaron para hacer vino. Luego hicieron una fiesta. Entraron en el templo de su dios, y allí comieron, bebieron y maldijeron a Abimelec.

decisions.choice: a festival of praise: the thanksgiving feast at the grape harvest
decisions.reason: The word means praises or rejoicing, and is used of fruit set apart to give thanks at harvest (Leviticus 19:24). When the grapes had been gathered and trodden, the people feasted in the temple.

decisions.choice: the house of their god: the temple of Baal-berith
decisions.reason: Their god is Baal-berith (verse 4; 8:33), also called El-berith (verse 46). The feast that ought to thank God is held in Baal's house, and turns into a feast of cursing.

decisions.choice: temple
decisions.reason: As in verse 4, "house" of a god is its temple.

decisions.choice: At harvest time ... to make wine
decisions.reason: Readable explains what gathering and treading the grapes meant.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀גַּ֣עַל בֶּן־עֶ֗בֶד מִֽי־אֲבִימֶ֤לֶךְ וּמִֽי־שְׁכֶם֙ כִּ֣י נַעַבְדֶ֔נּוּ הֲלֹ֥א בֶן־יְרֻבַּ֖עַל וּזְבֻ֣ל פְּקִיד֑וֹ עִבְד֗וּ אֶת־אַנְשֵׁ֤י חֲמוֹר֙ אֲבִ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם וּמַדּ֖וּעַ נַעַבְדֶ֥נּוּ אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Gaal son of Ebed, who [is] Abimelech and who [is] Shechem, that we should serve him? [Is he] not [the] son of Jerubbaal, and Zebul his officer? Serve [the] men of Hamor, [the] father of Shechem! And why should we serve him, we?

en.L: And Gaal son of Ebed said, "Who [is] Abimelech, and who [is] Shechem, that we should serve him? [Is he] not the son of Jerubbaal, and [is not] Zebul his officer? Serve the men of Hamor the father of Shechem! Why should we serve him?
en.B: Gaal son of Ebed said, "Who is Abimelech, and what is Shechem, that we should be his servants? Is he not Jerubbaal's son, with Zebul as his deputy? Serve the men of Hamor, Shechem's father! Why should we serve Abimelech?
en.R: Gaal son of Ebed said, "Who is this Abimelech? And who are we in Shechem, that we should serve him? He is only Jerubbaal's son, and Zebul is only his deputy! Serve the family of Hamor, the father of Shechem! Why should we serve Abimelech?

sw.L: Naye Gaali mwana wa Ebedi akasema, "Abimeleki [ni] nani, na Shekemu [ni] nani, hata tumtumikie? Je, [yeye si] mwana wa Yerubaali, na Zebuli [si] msimamizi wake? Watumikieni watu wa Hamori baba wa Shekemu! Kwa nini sisi tumtumikie yeye?
sw.B: Gaali mwana wa Ebedi alisema, "Abimeleki ni nani, na Shekemu ni nini, hata tuwe watumishi wake? Je, yeye si mwana wa Yerubaali, na Zebuli ni msaidizi wake? Watumikieni watu wa Hamori, baba wa Shekemu! Kwa nini tumtumikie Abimeleki?
sw.R: Gaali mwana wa Ebedi alisema, "Huyu Abimeleki ni nani? Na sisi watu wa Shekemu ni nani, hata tumtumikie? Yeye ni mwana wa Yerubaali tu, na Zebuli ni msaidizi wake tu! Itumikieni jamaa ya Hamori, baba wa Shekemu! Kwa nini tumtumikie Abimeleki?

es.L: Y dijo Gaal hijo de Ebed: «¿Quién [es] Abimelec, y quién [es] Siquem, para que le sirvamos? ¿No [es] el hijo de Jerobaal, y Zebul su oficial? {{plural_you:Sirvan|Servid}} a los hombres de Hamor, padre de Siquem. ¿Por qué hemos de servirle nosotros?
es.B: Gaal hijo de Ebed dijo: «¿Quién es Abimelec, y qué es Siquem, para que seamos sus siervos? ¿No es él hijo de Jerobaal, y Zebul su lugarteniente? ¡{{plural_you:Sirvan|Servid}} a los hombres de Hamor, el padre de Siquem! ¿Por qué hemos de servir a Abimelec?
es.R: Gaal hijo de Ebed dijo: «¿Quién se cree este Abimelec? ¿Y quiénes somos nosotros en Siquem para servirle? ¡No es más que el hijo de Jerobaal, y Zebul no es más que su lugarteniente! ¡{{plural_you:Sirvan|Servid}} a la familia de Hamor, el padre de Siquem! ¿Por qué hemos de servir a Abimelec?

decisions.choice: who is Shechem: what is Shechem, that it should serve such a man?
alternatives: who is the son of Shechem
decisions.reason: Gaal sets the city's name beside Abimelech's: Shechem, an old and proud city, should not be the servant of Jerubbaal's son. Others take "Shechem" to point to Abimelech himself, as the man of Shechem by his mother, or read the line with a small change as "who is the son of Shechem". The sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: serve the men of Hamor: a command in the Hebrew
alternatives: they served the men of Hamor
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "serve!", urging the city to obey the old ruling family of Shechem rather than Abimelech. The Greek translation reads "he served" or "they served", making it a statement: Jerubbaal's house once served Hamor's men. The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: Hamor the father of Shechem: the city's first ruling family
decisions.reason: Hamor was the Hivite prince of Shechem in Jacob's day, and his son was named Shechem (Genesis 33:19; 34:2). Gaal stirs up pride in the old native families against Abimelech, whose father was an Israelite from Ophrah.

decisions.choice: Zebul his officer: the governor Abimelech had put over the city
decisions.reason: The word means one appointed or put in charge, a deputy (Genesis 41:34). Verse 30 calls Zebul the ruler of the city.

decisions.choice: who are we in Shechem
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense chosen in m1, that the city's own standing is meant.

decisions.choice: Abimelech
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Abimelech for "him" at the end, where several men have just been named.

source.text: וּמִ֨י יִתֵּ֜ן אֶת־הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ בְּיָדִ֔י וְאָסִ֖ירָה אֶת־אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לַאֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ רַבֶּ֥ה צְבָאֲךָ֖ וָצֵֽאָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And who would give this people into my hand! And I would remove Abimelech. And he said to Abimelech, increase your army and come out.

en.L: If only this people were in my hand! Then I would remove Abimelech." And he said to Abimelech, "Increase your army and come out."
en.B: If only this people were under my command! I would get rid of Abimelech." And he said to Abimelech, "Build up your army and come out and fight!"
en.R: If only I were the leader of these people! I would get rid of Abimelech." Then Gaal shouted a challenge to Abimelech: "Gather your army and come out and fight!"

sw.L: Laiti watu hawa wangekuwa mkononi mwangu! Ndipo ningemwondoa Abimeleki." Naye akamwambia Abimeleki, "Ongeza jeshi lako utoke."
sw.B: Laiti watu hawa wangekuwa chini ya uongozi wangu! Ningemwondoa Abimeleki." Naye akamwambia Abimeleki, "Liimarishe jeshi lako, utoke upigane!"
sw.R: Laiti mimi ningekuwa kiongozi wa watu hawa! Ningemwondoa Abimeleki." Kisha Gaali akampa Abimeleki changamoto kwa sauti: "Likusanye jeshi lako, utoke upigane!"

es.L: ¡Quién pusiera a este pueblo en mi mano! Entonces yo quitaría a Abimelec.» Y dijo a Abimelec: «Aumenta tu ejército y sal.»
es.B: ¡Si este pueblo estuviera bajo mi mando! Yo me libraría de Abimelec.» Y le dijo a Abimelec: «¡Refuerza tu ejército y sal a pelear!»
es.R: ¡Si yo fuera el jefe de esta gente! Me libraría de Abimelec.» Luego Gaal le lanzó un desafío a Abimelec: «¡Reúne tu ejército y sal a pelear!»

decisions.choice: who would give this people into my hand: if only I had command of them
decisions.reason: "Who will give ...?" is the usual Hebrew way of saying "if only" (Numbers 11:29; 2 Samuel 19:1). "Into my hand" means under my control.

decisions.choice: and he said to Abimelech: Gaal's challenge, spoken against an absent rival
alternatives: and I would say to Abimelech
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he said". The Greek translation reads "and I would say", which makes the challenge part of Gaal's boast; the two differ by one letter. Abimelech is not in the city (verse 31), so in the Hebrew the challenge is a taunt for others to carry to him. The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: increase your army and come out: a dare to come and fight
decisions.reason: "Come out" is the word for marching out to battle (verses 33, 38).

decisions.choice: and fight
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "and fight" to make the challenge clear.

decisions.choice: shouted a challenge
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the words are a challenge thrown out, not a message delivered (m2).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֗ע זְבֻל֙ שַׂר־הָעִ֔יר אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֖י גַּ֣עַל בֶּן־עָ֑בֶד וַיִּ֖חַר אַפּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard Zebul, [the] ruler of the city, [the] words of Gaal son of Ebed, and burned his anger.

en.L: And Zebul, the ruler of the city, heard the words of Gaal son of Ebed, and his anger burned.
en.B: When Zebul, the governor of the city, heard what Gaal son of Ebed had said, he was furious.
en.R: Zebul, the man in charge of the city, heard what Gaal said, and he became very angry.

sw.L: Naye Zebuli, mtawala wa mji, akasikia maneno ya Gaali mwana wa Ebedi, na hasira yake ikawaka.
sw.B: Zebuli, liwali wa mji, aliposikia yale Gaali mwana wa Ebedi aliyosema, alikasirika sana.
sw.R: Zebuli, mtu aliyesimamia mji, alisikia yale Gaali aliyosema, akakasirika sana.

es.L: Y Zebul, el gobernador de la ciudad, oyó las palabras de Gaal hijo de Ebed, y se encendió su ira.
es.B: Cuando Zebul, el gobernador de la ciudad, oyó lo que había dicho Gaal hijo de Ebed, se enfureció.
es.R: Zebul, el hombre que estaba a cargo de la ciudad, oyó lo que dijo Gaal, y se enojó mucho.

decisions.choice: the ruler of the city: the governor who ran Shechem for Abimelech
decisions.reason: The word sar names an official with power over others. "The sar of the city" is its governor (1 Kings 22:26; 2 Kings 23:8). Zebul is Abimelech's deputy (verse 28), loyal to him while Abimelech lives elsewhere (verse 41).

decisions.choice: his anger burned: he became very angry
decisions.reason: Anger is pictured as heat in the face or nostrils, a common Hebrew way of speaking (Genesis 30:2; Exodus 32:19).

decisions.choice: ruler (L), governor (B), the man in charge (R)
decisions.reason: Here sar is the head of a city, not a court official or an army commander, so "prince" and "commander" do not fit. Literal says "ruler", Balanced "governor", Readable "the man in charge".

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֧ח מַלְאָכִ֛ים אֶל־אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ בְּתָרְמָ֣ה לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּה֩ גַ֨עַל בֶּן־עֶ֤בֶד וְאֶחָיו֙ בָּאִ֣ים שְׁכֶ֔מָה וְהִנָּ֛ם צָרִ֥ים אֶת־הָעִ֖יר עָלֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he sent messengers to Abimelech in deceit, saying, look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers [are] coming to Shechem, and look, they [are] stirring up the city against you.

en.L: And he sent messengers to Abimelech in secret, saying, "Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem, and look, they are stirring up the city against you.
en.B: He secretly sent messengers to Abimelech to say, "Gaal son of Ebed and his relatives have come to Shechem, and they are turning the city against you.
en.R: He secretly sent messengers to Abimelech with this message: "Gaal son of Ebed and his relatives have come to Shechem. They are turning the people of the city against you.

sw.L: Naye akatuma wajumbe kwa Abimeleki kwa siri, akisema, "Tazama, Gaali mwana wa Ebedi na ndugu zake wamekuja Shekemu, na tazama, wanauchochea mji dhidi yako.
sw.B: Alituma wajumbe kwa Abimeleki kwa siri kusema, "Gaali mwana wa Ebedi na jamaa zake wamekuja Shekemu, nao wanaugeuza mji dhidi yako.
sw.R: Alituma wajumbe kwa Abimeleki kwa siri na ujumbe huu: "Gaali mwana wa Ebedi na jamaa zake wamekuja Shekemu. Wanawageuza watu wa mji dhidi yako.

es.L: Y envió mensajeros a Abimelec en secreto, diciendo: «Mira, Gaal hijo de Ebed y sus hermanos han venido a Siquem, y he aquí, están sublevando la ciudad contra ti.
es.B: En secreto envió mensajeros a Abimelec para decirle: «Gaal hijo de Ebed y sus parientes han venido a Siquem, y están poniendo la ciudad en contra tuya.
es.R: En secreto envió mensajeros a Abimelec con este mensaje: «Gaal hijo de Ebed y sus parientes han venido a Siquem. Están poniendo a la gente de la ciudad en contra tuya.

decisions.choice: in deceit: secretly, by stealth
decisions.reason: The word means deceit or trickery: Zebul acts behind Gaal's back while pretending to be on his side (verses 36-38). Some take it as a place name, "at Tormah", perhaps the same as Arumah (verse 41), where Abimelech was staying.

decisions.choice: stirring up the city against you: turning the city to hostility
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to besiege or shut in. Said of a city "against" its ruler, it may mean rousing it to revolt, or shutting its gates against him. Either way Shechem is being closed to Abimelech.

decisions.choice: "look" left out
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out the two "look"s, which mark urgent news in Hebrew; the plain wording and the haste of the message carry it. Literal keeps them.

source.text: וְעַתָּה֙ ק֣וּם לַ֔יְלָה אַתָּ֖ה וְהָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתָּ֑ךְ וֶאֱרֹ֖ב בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, arise by night, you and the people who [are] with you, and lie in wait in the field.

en.L: And now, rise up by night, you and the people who [are] with you, and lie in wait in the field.
en.B: So now, set out during the night, you and the troops with you, and lie in ambush in the open country.
en.R: So come during the night with your men and hide in the fields outside the city.

sw.L: Basi sasa, ondoka usiku, wewe na watu [walio] pamoja nawe, mkavizie shambani.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo sasa, ondoka usiku, wewe na askari walio pamoja nawe, mkavizie katika mashamba nje ya mji.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo njoo usiku pamoja na watu wako, mjifiche mashambani nje ya mji.

es.L: Y ahora, levántate de noche, tú y el pueblo que [está] contigo, y pon emboscada en el campo.
es.B: Así que ahora, ponte en marcha durante la noche, tú y las tropas que están contigo, y tiéndeles una emboscada en el campo abierto.
es.R: Así que ven durante la noche con tus hombres y escóndete en los campos fuera de la ciudad.

decisions.choice: the people with you: your fighting men
decisions.reason: "The people" here are Abimelech's troops, as often in battle stories (Exodus 14:6; Joshua 8:1).

decisions.choice: the field: the open country outside the city walls
decisions.reason: "The field" is the land outside a town, its farmland and pasture, where men could hide among the crops and terraces.

decisions.choice: troops / men
decisions.reason: Balanced says "troops" and Readable "men" for "the people" in the sense of m1; Literal keeps "the people". The same is done through the battle that follows.

source.text: וְהָיָ֤ה בַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ כִּזְרֹ֣חַ הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ תַּשְׁכִּ֖ים וּפָשַׁטְתָּ֣ עַל־הָעִ֑יר וְהִנֵּה־ה֞וּא וְהָעָ֤ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּוֹ֙ יֹצְאִ֣ים אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר תִּמְצָ֥א יָדֶֽךָ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it will be in the morning, as the sun rises, you will rise early and rush upon the city; and look, he and the people who [are] with him [are] going out against you, and you will do to him as your hand finds.

en.L: And in the morning, as the sun rises, rise early and rush upon the city; and look, [when] he and the people who [are] with him come out against you, you will do to him whatever your hand finds."
en.B: In the morning, as soon as the sun is up, get up early and charge the city. When he and his men come out against you, deal with him however the moment allows."
en.R: Then early in the morning, at sunrise, attack the city. When Gaal and his men come out to fight you, do whatever you need to do to him."

sw.L: Na asubuhi, jua linapochomoza, amka mapema uushambulie mji ghafla; na tazama, [atakapotoka] yeye na watu [walio] pamoja naye dhidi yako, utamtendea lolote mkono wako utakaloona."
sw.B: Asubuhi, mara jua linapochomoza, amka mapema uushambulie mji. Yeye na watu wake watakapotoka dhidi yako, mtendee kadiri nafasi itakavyokuruhusu."
sw.R: Kisha asubuhi na mapema, jua linapochomoza, ushambulie mji. Gaali na watu wake watakapotoka kupigana nawe, mtendee lolote unalohitaji kumtendea."

es.L: Y por la mañana, al salir el sol, madrugarás y caerás sobre la ciudad; y he aquí, [cuando] él y el pueblo que [está] con él salgan contra ti, harás con él lo que halle tu mano.»
es.B: Por la mañana, en cuanto salga el sol, levántate temprano y lánzate contra la ciudad. Cuando él y sus hombres salgan contra ti, haz con él lo que la ocasión te permita.»
es.R: Luego, temprano por la mañana, al salir el sol, ataca la ciudad. Cuando Gaal y sus hombres salgan a pelear contra ti, haz con él lo que tengas que hacer.»

decisions.choice: do to him as your hand finds: do whatever you have the chance and the power to do
decisions.reason: "As your hand finds" means as opportunity and strength allow (1 Samuel 10:7; 25:8). Zebul leaves the details of the fight to Abimelech.

decisions.choice: rush upon the city: make a sudden attack
decisions.reason: The verb means to spread out or dash, used of raiding parties falling on a place (verse 44; 1 Samuel 23:27).

decisions.choice: Gaal
decisions.reason: Readable names Gaal for "he".

decisions.choice: [when]
decisions.reason: Literal adds "when" in brackets, since the Hebrew "look, he ... going out" pictures what will happen once the attack begins.

source.text: וַיָּ֧קָם אֲבִימֶ֛לֶךְ וְכָל־הָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־עִמּ֖וֹ לָ֑יְלָה וַיֶּאֶרְב֣וּ עַל־שְׁכֶ֔ם אַרְבָּעָ֖ה רָאשִֽׁים׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose Abimelech and all the people who [were] with him by night, and lay in wait against Shechem [in] four companies.

en.L: And Abimelech and all the people who [were] with him rose up by night and lay in wait against Shechem [in] four companies.
en.B: So Abimelech and all the troops with him set out by night and took up hidden positions around Shechem in four companies.
en.R: So Abimelech and all his men came during the night. They split into four groups and hid near Shechem.

sw.L: Naye Abimeleki na watu wote [waliokuwa] pamoja naye wakaondoka usiku, wakavizia dhidi ya Shekemu [katika] vikosi vinne.
sw.B: Basi Abimeleki na askari wote waliokuwa pamoja naye waliondoka usiku, wakajificha kuizunguka Shekemu katika vikosi vinne.
sw.R: Basi Abimeleki na watu wake wote walikuja usiku. Walijigawa katika makundi manne, wakajificha karibu na Shekemu.

es.L: Y se levantó Abimelec y todo el pueblo que [estaba] con él de noche, y pusieron emboscada contra Siquem [en] cuatro compañías.
es.B: Así que Abimelec y todas las tropas que estaban con él se pusieron en marcha de noche y se escondieron alrededor de Siquem en cuatro compañías.
es.R: Así que Abimelec y todos sus hombres llegaron durante la noche. Se dividieron en cuatro grupos y se escondieron cerca de Siquem.

decisions.choice: four companies: four units of the army
decisions.reason: The word is "heads", used of the divisions of a fighting force (7:16; 1 Samuel 11:11). Each lay hidden on a different side of the city.

decisions.choice: troops / men
decisions.reason: As in verse 32, "the people" with Abimelech are his fighting men: "troops" at Balanced, "men" at Readable.

source.text: וַיֵּצֵא֙ גַּ֣עַל בֶּן־עֶ֔בֶד וַיַּעֲמֹ֕ד פֶּ֖תַח שַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֑יר וַיָּ֧קָם אֲבִימֶ֛לֶךְ וְהָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֖וֹ מִן־הַמַּאְרָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out Gaal son of Ebed and stood [at the] entrance of [the] gate of the city, and arose Abimelech and the people who [were] with him from the ambush.

en.L: And Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood at the entrance of the gate of the city, and Abimelech and the people who [were] with him rose up from the ambush.
en.B: Gaal son of Ebed went out and was standing at the entrance to the city gate when Abimelech and his troops rose up from their hiding places.
en.R: Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood at the city gate. Just then Abimelech and his men came out of their hiding places.

sw.L: Naye Gaali mwana wa Ebedi akatoka, akasimama penye mlango wa lango la mji, naye Abimeleki na watu [waliokuwa] pamoja naye wakainuka kutoka mavizioni.
sw.B: Gaali mwana wa Ebedi alitoka akasimama penye mlango wa lango la mji wakati Abimeleki na askari wake walipoinuka kutoka mahali walipojificha.
sw.R: Gaali mwana wa Ebedi alitoka akasimama penye lango la mji. Wakati huo huo Abimeleki na watu wake walitoka mahali walipojificha.

es.L: Y salió Gaal hijo de Ebed y se puso a la entrada de la puerta de la ciudad, y Abimelec y el pueblo que [estaba] con él se levantaron de la emboscada.
es.B: Gaal hijo de Ebed salió y estaba de pie a la entrada de la puerta de la ciudad cuando Abimelec y sus tropas salieron de sus escondites.
es.R: Gaal hijo de Ebed salió y se quedó de pie en la puerta de la ciudad. En ese momento Abimelec y sus hombres salieron de sus escondites.

decisions.choice: the entrance of the city gate: the place of public business and of defense
decisions.reason: The gate was where a city's leaders sat to settle its affairs (Ruth 4:1; 2 Samuel 15:2) and where it was defended. Gaal stands there as the man now in charge of Shechem.

decisions.choice: troops / men
decisions.reason: As in verse 32, "the people" with Abimelech are his fighting men: "troops" at Balanced, "men" at Readable.

decisions.choice: Just then
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the two things happen at the same moment, as the Hebrew order implies.

source.text: וַיַּרְא־גַּעַל֮ אֶת־הָעָם֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־זְבֻ֔ל הִנֵּה־עָ֣ם יוֹרֵ֔ד מֵרָאשֵׁ֖י הֶהָרִ֑ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ זְבֻ֔ל אֵ֣ת צֵ֧ל הֶהָרִ֛ים אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה כָּאֲנָשִֽׁים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And saw Gaal the people and said to Zebul, look, people coming down from [the] tops of the mountains. And said to him Zebul, [the] shadow of the mountains you [are] seeing as men.

en.L: And Gaal saw the people and said to Zebul, "Look, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains." And Zebul said to him, "You are seeing the shadow of the mountains as [if they were] men."
en.B: When Gaal saw the troops, he said to Zebul, "Look, there are people coming down from the mountaintops!" Zebul answered, "You are taking the shadows of the mountains for men."
en.R: Gaal saw them and said to Zebul, "Look! People are coming down from the tops of the hills!" But Zebul told him, "Those are only the shadows on the hills. They just look like men to you."

sw.L: Naye Gaali akawaona watu, akamwambia Zebuli, "Tazama, watu wanashuka kutoka vilele vya milima." Naye Zebuli akamwambia, "Unaona kivuli cha milima kama [kwamba ni] watu."
sw.B: Gaali alipowaona askari, alimwambia Zebuli, "Tazama, watu wanashuka kutoka vilele vya milima!" Zebuli akamjibu, "Unadhani vivuli vya milima ni watu."
sw.R: Gaali aliwaona, akamwambia Zebuli, "Tazama! Watu wanashuka kutoka vilele vya vilima!" Lakini Zebuli akamwambia, "Hivyo ni vivuli tu vya vilima. Wanaonekana kwako kama watu tu."

es.L: Y Gaal vio al pueblo y dijo a Zebul: «Mira, gente desciende de las cumbres de los montes.» Y Zebul le dijo: «Tú ves la sombra de los montes como [si fueran] hombres.»
es.B: Cuando Gaal vio a las tropas, le dijo a Zebul: «¡Mira, viene gente bajando de las cumbres de los montes!» Zebul le respondió: «Estás confundiendo las sombras de los montes con hombres.»
es.R: Gaal los vio y le dijo a Zebul: «¡Mira! ¡Viene gente bajando de lo alto de las colinas!» Pero Zebul le dijo: «No son más que las sombras de las colinas. Solo te parecen hombres.»

decisions.choice: the shadow of the mountains: shapes in the early light that look like men
decisions.reason: It is sunrise (verse 33), when the shadows on the slopes are long. Zebul, secretly on Abimelech's side (verse 31), makes light of what Gaal sees, to give Abimelech's men time to come close.

decisions.choice: Zebul is with Gaal at the gate
decisions.reason: Zebul stays beside Gaal as if he were an ally. His mocking reply in verse 38 shows that he has played for time on purpose.

decisions.choice: only ... They just look like men
decisions.reason: Readable brings out Zebul's dismissive tone.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨סֶף ע֣וֹד גַּעַל֮ לְדַבֵּר֒ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּה־עָם֙ יֽוֹרְדִ֔ים מֵעִ֖ם טַבּ֣וּר הָאָ֑רֶץ וְרֹאשׁ־אֶחָ֣ד בָּ֔א מִדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֵל֥וֹן מְעוֹנְנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And again yet Gaal spoke and said, look, people coming down from with [the] navel of the land, and one company coming from [the] way of [the] oak of [the] soothsayers.

en.L: And Gaal spoke again and said, "Look, people are coming down from the navel of the land, and one company is coming by the way of the oak of the soothsayers."
en.B: Gaal spoke again: "Look, troops are coming down from the center of the land, and another company is coming by the road from the Soothsayers' Oak!"
en.R: Gaal spoke again: "Look! Men are coming down from the high ground in the middle of the land! And another group is coming along the road from the Fortune-tellers' Oak!"

sw.L: Naye Gaali akasema tena, akasema, "Tazama, watu wanashuka kutoka kitovu cha nchi, na kikosi kimoja kinakuja kwa njia ya mwaloni wa wapiga ramli."
sw.B: Gaali akasema tena, "Tazama, askari wanashuka kutoka katikati ya nchi, na kikosi kingine kinakuja kwa njia itokayo Mwaloni wa Wapiga Ramli!"
sw.R: Gaali akasema tena, "Tazama! Watu wanashuka kutoka nchi ya juu iliyo katikati ya nchi! Na kundi lingine linakuja kwa njia itokayo Mwaloni wa Waaguzi!"

es.L: Y volvió Gaal a hablar y dijo: «Mira, gente desciende del ombligo de la tierra, y una compañía viene por el camino de la encina de los adivinos.»
es.B: Gaal volvió a hablar: «¡Mira, vienen tropas bajando del centro de la tierra, y otra compañía viene por el camino de la Encina de los Adivinos!»
es.R: Gaal volvió a hablar: «¡Mira! ¡Vienen hombres bajando de la parte alta que está en medio de la tierra! ¡Y otro grupo viene por el camino de la Encina de los Adivinos!»

decisions.choice: the navel of the land: a high point at the center of the land
decisions.reason: The word means navel, and is used of the land as the center of the world (Ezekiel 38:12). Here it is probably a hill near Shechem thought of as the middle of the land, perhaps a shoulder of Mount Gerizim. Its place is not known.

decisions.choice: the oak of the soothsayers: a tree where people sought omens
decisions.reason: Soothsayers read signs to tell the future, a practice the law forbids (Deuteronomy 18:10, 14). The tree was a known landmark near Shechem; it may be the same as the "oak of Moreh", "oak of the teacher", where Abraham camped (Genesis 12:6).

decisions.choice: troops
decisions.reason: Balanced says "troops" for "people" here, since Gaal is now seeing armed men; Readable says "men".

decisions.choice: the Soothsayers' Oak / the Fortune-tellers' Oak
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable write the landmark as a name. Readable says "fortune-tellers", a commoner word for the same people.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו זְבֻ֗ל אַיֵּ֨ה אֵפ֥וֹא פִ֨יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֹּאמַ֔ר מִ֥י אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ כִּ֣י נַעַבְדֶ֑נּוּ הֲלֹ֨א זֶ֤ה הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָאַ֣סְתָּה בּ֔וֹ צֵא־נָ֥א עַתָּ֖ה וְהִלָּ֥חֶם בּֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said to him Zebul, where [is] then your mouth, which you said, who [is] Abimelech that we should serve him? [Is] not this the people that you despised? Go out, please, now and fight against it.

en.L: And Zebul said to him, "Where then [is] your mouth, with which you said, 'Who [is] Abimelech, that we should serve him?' [Is] not this the people that you despised? Go out now, please, and fight against them."
en.B: Then Zebul said to him, "Where is your big talk now, you who said, 'Who is Abimelech, that we should be his servants?' Are these not the men you looked down on? Go out now and fight them!"
en.R: Then Zebul said to him, "Where is all your bragging now? You said, 'Who is Abimelech? Why should we serve him?' These are the men you made fun of! Go out and fight them now!"

sw.L: Naye Zebuli akamwambia, "Kiko wapi basi kinywa chako, ulichosema kwacho, 'Abimeleki [ni] nani, hata tumtumikie?' Je, hawa [si] watu uliowadharau? Tafadhali toka sasa upigane nao."
sw.B: Kisha Zebuli alimwambia, "Yako wapi sasa majivuno yako, wewe uliyesema, 'Abimeleki ni nani, hata tuwe watumishi wake?' Je, hawa si wale watu uliowadharau? Toka sasa upigane nao!"
sw.R: Kisha Zebuli akamwambia, "Uko wapi sasa ule ujigambo wako wote? Ulisema, 'Abimeleki ni nani? Kwa nini tumtumikie?' Hawa ndio watu uliowadhihaki! Toka nje upigane nao sasa!"

es.L: Y Zebul le dijo: «¿Dónde [está] ahora tu boca, con la que decías: “¿Quién [es] Abimelec para que le sirvamos?” ¿No [es] este el pueblo que despreciaste? Sal ahora, por favor, y pelea contra él.»
es.B: Entonces Zebul le dijo: «¿Dónde están ahora tus fanfarronadas, tú que decías: “¿Quién es Abimelec para que seamos sus siervos?” ¿No son estos los hombres que despreciaste? ¡Sal ahora y pelea contra ellos!»
es.R: Entonces Zebul le dijo: «¿Dónde quedaron ahora todas tus fanfarronadas? Tú decías: “¿Quién es Abimelec? ¿Por qué tenemos que servirle?” ¡Estos son los hombres de los que te burlabas! ¡Sal ahora y pelea contra ellos!»

decisions.choice: where is your mouth: what has become of your boasting?
decisions.reason: "Mouth" stands for what Gaal said. Zebul quotes Gaal's own words back to him (verse 28) and now drops his pretense.

decisions.choice: despised: rejected with scorn
decisions.reason: The verb means to reject or treat as worthless (1 Samuel 8:7; 15:23). Gaal had scorned Abimelech and his following.

decisions.choice: your big talk
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of "your mouth" (m1); Literal keeps "your mouth", Readable says "your bragging".

source.text: וַיֵּ֣צֵא גַ֔עַל לִפְנֵ֖י בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֑ם וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם בַּאֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out Gaal before [the] lords of Shechem and fought against Abimelech.

en.L: And Gaal went out before the lords of Shechem and fought against Abimelech.
en.B: So Gaal went out at the head of the leaders of Shechem and fought Abimelech.
en.R: So Gaal led the leaders of Shechem out of the city and fought against Abimelech.

sw.L: Naye Gaali akatoka mbele ya wakuu wa Shekemu, akapigana na Abimeleki.
sw.B: Basi Gaali alitoka akiwaongoza viongozi wa Shekemu, akapigana na Abimeleki.
sw.R: Basi Gaali aliwaongoza viongozi wa Shekemu kutoka nje ya mji, akapigana na Abimeleki.

es.L: Y salió Gaal delante de los señores de Siquem, y peleó contra Abimelec.
es.B: Así que Gaal salió al frente de los líderes de Siquem y peleó contra Abimelec.
es.R: Así que Gaal sacó de la ciudad a los líderes de Siquem y peleó contra Abimelec.

decisions.choice: before the lords of Shechem: at their head, leading them
alternatives: in the sight of the lords of Shechem
decisions.reason: "Before" can mean in front of them, leading them into battle, or in their sight, while they watched from the city. Leading them fits best, since Gaal has claimed to be their leader (verse 29).

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

source.text: וַיִּרְדְּפֵ֣הוּ אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ וַיָּ֖נָס מִפָּנָ֑יו וַֽיִּפְּל֛וּ חֲלָלִ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים עַד־פֶּ֥תַח הַשָּֽׁעַר׃

records.literal_gloss: And pursued him Abimelech, and he fled from before him, and fell slain many to [the] entrance of the gate.

en.L: And Abimelech pursued him, and he fled before him, and many fell slain, up to the entrance of the gate.
en.B: Abimelech chased him, and Gaal ran from him. Many fell dead along the way, right up to the entrance of the gate.
en.R: Abimelech chased Gaal, and Gaal ran away from him. Many of Gaal's men were killed on the way back to the city gate.

sw.L: Naye Abimeleki akamfuatia, naye akakimbia mbele yake, na wengi wakaanguka wameuawa, hata mpaka mlangoni mwa lango.
sw.B: Abimeleki alimfukuza, naye Gaali akamkimbia. Wengi walianguka wamekufa njiani, mpaka penye mlango wa lango.
sw.R: Abimeleki alimfukuza Gaali, naye Gaali akamkimbia. Watu wengi wa Gaali waliuawa njiani walipokuwa wakirudi kwenye lango la mji.

es.L: Y Abimelec lo persiguió, y él huyó delante de él, y cayeron muchos heridos hasta la entrada de la puerta.
es.B: Abimelec lo persiguió, y Gaal huyó de él. Muchos cayeron muertos por el camino, hasta la entrada misma de la puerta.
es.R: Abimelec persiguió a Gaal, y Gaal huyó de él. Muchos de los hombres de Gaal murieron en el camino de regreso a la puerta de la ciudad.

decisions.choice: slain: struck down, killed or fatally wounded
decisions.reason: The word means pierced, those struck down in battle (Deuteronomy 21:1). The rout reaches the very gate from which Gaal had gone out.

decisions.choice: Gaal
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Gaal where the Hebrew says "he"; Readable also makes clear that the dead were Gaal's men.

source.text: וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ בָּארוּמָ֑ה וַיְגָ֧רֶשׁ זְבֻ֛ל אֶת־גַּ֥עַל וְאֶת־אֶחָ֖יו מִשֶּׁ֥בֶת בִּשְׁכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And stayed Abimelech at Arumah, and drove out Zebul Gaal and his brothers from dwelling in Shechem.

en.L: And Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul drove out Gaal and his brothers from living in Shechem.
en.B: Abimelech then stayed at Arumah, and Zebul drove Gaal and his relatives out, so that they could no longer live in Shechem.
en.R: Abimelech stayed in the town of Arumah. Zebul forced Gaal and his relatives to leave Shechem.

sw.L: Naye Abimeleki akakaa Aruma, naye Zebuli akawafukuza Gaali na ndugu zake wasikae Shekemu.
sw.B: Kisha Abimeleki alikaa Aruma, naye Zebuli akawafukuza Gaali na jamaa zake, wasiweze tena kukaa Shekemu.
sw.R: Abimeleki alikaa katika mji wa Aruma. Zebuli aliwalazimisha Gaali na jamaa zake kuondoka Shekemu.

es.L: Y Abimelec se quedó en Aruma, y Zebul expulsó a Gaal y a sus hermanos para que no habitaran en Siquem.
es.B: Abimelec se quedó entonces en Aruma, y Zebul echó a Gaal y a sus parientes, de modo que ya no pudieron vivir en Siquem.
es.R: Abimelec se quedó en la ciudad de Aruma. Zebul obligó a Gaal y a sus parientes a irse de Siquem.

decisions.choice: Arumah: a town near Shechem, perhaps Abimelech's base
decisions.reason: Arumah is not named anywhere else; it was probably a few miles from Shechem. Abimelech does not live in Shechem itself but rules it through Zebul (verses 28, 30).

decisions.choice: relatives
decisions.reason: As in verse 26.

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיֵּצֵ֥א הָעָ֖ם הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַיַּגִּ֖דוּ לַאֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was on the next day, and went out the people [to] the field, and they told Abimelech.

en.L: And it happened on the next day that the people went out into the field, and they told Abimelech.
en.B: On the following day the people of Shechem came out to the fields, and someone reported it to Abimelech.
en.R: The next day the people of Shechem went out to work in their fields. Someone told Abimelech about it.

sw.L: Ikawa kesho yake watu wakatoka kwenda shambani, nao wakamwambia Abimeleki.
sw.B: Siku iliyofuata watu wa Shekemu walitoka kwenda mashambani, na mtu fulani akampelekea Abimeleki habari hiyo.
sw.R: Kesho yake watu wa Shekemu walitoka kwenda kufanya kazi mashambani mwao. Mtu fulani alimwambia Abimeleki habari hiyo.

es.L: Y sucedió al día siguiente que el pueblo salió al campo, y se lo avisaron a Abimelec.
es.B: Al día siguiente la gente de Siquem salió a los campos, y alguien se lo informó a Abimelec.
