es.R: Al día siguiente la gente de Siquem salió a trabajar en sus campos. Alguien se lo contó a Abimelec.

decisions.choice: the people: the people of Shechem, not Abimelech's troops
decisions.reason: Here "the people" are the townspeople, who go out into the fields once Gaal has gone, perhaps thinking the danger is over. Abimelech treats it as a chance to strike.

decisions.choice: of Shechem
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose people are meant (m1).

decisions.choice: to work in
decisions.reason: Readable says why they went to the fields. The Hebrew does not say; work on the land is the likeliest reason, but they may have gone out armed.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־הָעָ֗ם וַֽיֶּחֱצֵם֙ לִשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה רָאשִׁ֔ים וַיֶּאֱרֹ֖ב בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֤ה הָעָם֙ יֹצֵ֣א מִן־הָעִ֔יר וַיָּ֥קָם עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם וַיַּכֵּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he took the people and divided them into three companies and lay in wait in the field; and he looked, and look, the people coming out from the city, and he rose against them and struck them.

en.L: And he took the people and divided them into three companies and lay in wait in the field. And he looked, and look, the people were coming out from the city, and he rose up against them and struck them.
en.B: He took his troops, split them into three companies, and set an ambush in the fields. As soon as he saw people leaving the city, he rose and attacked them.
en.R: Abimelech divided his army into three groups, and they hid in the fields. As soon as he saw people leaving the city, he jumped up and attacked them.

sw.L: Naye akawachukua watu, akawagawa katika vikosi vitatu, akavizia shambani. Akatazama, na tazama, watu walikuwa wakitoka mjini, naye akainuka dhidi yao, akawapiga.
sw.B: Aliwachukua askari wake, akawagawa katika vikosi vitatu, akaweka mavizio mashambani. Mara alipowaona watu wakitoka mjini, aliinuka akawashambulia.
sw.R: Abimeleki aligawa jeshi lake katika makundi matatu, nao wakajificha mashambani. Mara alipowaona watu wakitoka mjini, aliruka akawashambulia.

es.L: Y tomó al pueblo y lo dividió en tres compañías, y puso emboscada en el campo. Y miró, y he aquí, el pueblo salía de la ciudad, y se levantó contra ellos y los hirió.
es.B: Tomó a sus tropas, las dividió en tres compañías y les tendió una emboscada en los campos. En cuanto vio que la gente salía de la ciudad, se levantó y los atacó.
es.R: Abimelec dividió su ejército en tres grupos, y se escondieron en los campos. En cuanto vio que la gente salía de la ciudad, saltó de su escondite y los atacó.

decisions.choice: the people ... the people: first his troops, then the townspeople
decisions.reason: The same word is used twice in one verse with two meanings: the army Abimelech leads, and the people of Shechem coming out of the city (verse 42).

decisions.choice: troops / army
decisions.reason: As in verse 32, "the people" with Abimelech are his fighting men: "troops" at Balanced, "men" at Readable.

source.text: וַאֲבִימֶ֗לֶךְ וְהָרָאשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמּ֔וֹ פָּשְׁט֕וּ וַיַּ֣עַמְד֔וּ פֶּ֖תַח שַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֑יר וּשְׁנֵ֣י הָֽרָאשִׁ֗ים פָּֽשְׁט֛וּ עַֽל־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֖ה וַיַּכּֽוּם׃

records.literal_gloss: And Abimelech and the companies who [were] with him rushed and stood [at the] entrance of [the] gate of the city, and the two companies rushed upon all who [were] in the field and struck them.

en.L: And Abimelech and the companies that [were] with him rushed forward and stood at the entrance of the gate of the city, and the two [other] companies rushed upon all who [were] in the field and struck them.
en.B: Abimelech and the forces with him charged forward and took their stand at the entrance to the city gate, while the other two companies charged at everyone in the fields and struck them down.
en.R: Abimelech and the men with him rushed forward and took their place at the city gate, so that no one could get back in. The other two groups attacked the people in the fields and killed them.

sw.L: Naye Abimeleki na vikosi [vilivyokuwa] pamoja naye wakakimbia mbele, wakasimama penye mlango wa lango la mji, na vile vikosi viwili [vingine] vikawashambulia wote [waliokuwa] shambani, vikawapiga.
sw.B: Abimeleki na majeshi yaliyokuwa pamoja naye walikimbia mbele, wakasimama penye mlango wa lango la mji, huku vile vikosi viwili vingine vikiwashambulia wote waliokuwa mashambani na kuwaua.
sw.R: Abimeleki na watu waliokuwa pamoja naye walikimbia mbele wakashika lango la mji, ili mtu yeyote asiweze kurudi ndani. Yale makundi mawili mengine yaliwashambulia watu waliokuwa mashambani, yakawaua.

es.L: Y Abimelec y las compañías que [estaban] con él se lanzaron y se pusieron a la entrada de la puerta de la ciudad, y las dos [otras] compañías se lanzaron sobre todos los que [estaban] en el campo y los hirieron.
es.B: Abimelec y las fuerzas que lo acompañaban se lanzaron adelante y se apostaron a la entrada de la puerta de la ciudad, mientras las otras dos compañías se lanzaban contra todos los que estaban en los campos y los mataban.
es.R: Abimelec y los hombres que estaban con él se lanzaron adelante y se pusieron en la puerta de la ciudad, para que nadie pudiera volver a entrar. Los otros dos grupos atacaron a la gente que estaba en los campos y la mataron.

decisions.choice: the companies with him: one company with Abimelech, two in the fields
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the plural "companies", but verse 43 gives three companies and this verse sends "the two" against the fields, so only one can have been with Abimelech. Some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations have the singular "company". The plural may be a copying slip or a loose way of speaking; the sense is clear either way.

decisions.choice: standing at the gate: cutting off the way back into the city
decisions.reason: By holding the gate, Abimelech kept the people in the fields from escaping into Shechem while his other companies attacked them.

decisions.choice: the forces / the men with him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable do not repeat the plural "companies" here, which would make four companies in all; they say "forces" and "men" (m1). Literal keeps "companies".

decisions.choice: so that no one could get back in
decisions.reason: Readable says why Abimelech held the gate (m2).

source.text: וַאֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ נִלְחָ֣ם בָּעִ֗יר כֹּ֚ל הַיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וַיִּלְכֹּד֙ אֶת־הָעִ֔יר וְאֶת־הָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֖הּ הָרָ֑ג וַיִּתֹּץ֙ אֶת־הָעִ֔יר וַיִּזְרָעֶ֖הָ מֶֽלַח׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And Abimelech fought against the city all that day, and captured the city, and the people who [were] in it he killed, and he tore down the city and sowed it [with] salt.

en.L: And Abimelech fought against the city all that day, and he captured the city and killed the people who [were] in it, and he tore down the city and sowed it [with] salt.
en.B: Abimelech fought against the city all that day. He captured it and killed the people in it; then he tore the city down and scattered salt over it.
en.R: Abimelech fought against Shechem all day long. He captured the city and killed the people who were in it. Then he destroyed the city and spread salt over the ground.

sw.L: Naye Abimeleki akapigana na mji siku ile yote, akautwaa mji, akawaua watu [waliokuwa] ndani yake, akaubomoa mji, akaupanda [kwa] chumvi.
sw.B: Abimeleki alipigana na mji siku ile yote. Aliuteka, akawaua watu waliokuwa ndani yake; kisha akaubomoa mji, akanyunyiza chumvi juu yake.
sw.R: Abimeleki alipigana na Shekemu mchana kutwa. Aliuteka mji, akawaua watu waliokuwa ndani yake. Kisha akauharibu mji, akamwaga chumvi juu ya ardhi yake.

es.L: Y Abimelec peleó contra la ciudad todo aquel día, y tomó la ciudad, y mató al pueblo que [estaba] en ella; y asoló la ciudad y la sembró [de] sal.
es.B: Abimelec peleó contra la ciudad todo aquel día. La tomó y mató a la gente que había en ella; luego derribó la ciudad y esparció sal sobre ella.
es.R: Abimelec peleó contra Siquem todo el día. Tomó la ciudad y mató a la gente que estaba en ella. Luego destruyó la ciudad y echó sal sobre la tierra.

decisions.choice: sowed it with salt: marked it for lasting ruin
decisions.reason: Salt makes soil barren, and land "burned with salt" is a picture of ruin under a curse (Deuteronomy 29:22; Jeremiah 17:6). Scattering salt over the city was a sign that it should lie waste. The man who was made king in Shechem destroys it.

decisions.choice: he tore down the city: the town itself, while its tower still stood
decisions.reason: The Tower of Shechem is still held after this (verses 46-49), so the city's houses and walls are meant. Shechem was rebuilt long afterward (1 Kings 12:25).

decisions.choice: Shechem
decisions.reason: Readable names the city.

source.text: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֔וּ כָּֽל־בַּעֲלֵ֖י מִֽגְדַּל־שְׁכֶ֑ם וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אֶל־צְרִ֔יחַ בֵּ֖ית אֵ֥ל בְּרִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard all [the] lords of [the] Tower of Shechem, and they went into [the] stronghold of [the] house of El-berith.

en.L: And all the lords of the Tower of Shechem heard, and they went into the stronghold of the house of El-berith.
en.B: When all the leaders of the Tower of Shechem heard this, they went into the stronghold of the temple of El-berith.
en.R: All the leaders of the Tower of Shechem heard what had happened. So they went into the strong inner room of the temple of the god El-berith.

sw.L: Nao wakuu wote wa Mnara wa Shekemu wakasikia, wakaingia ndani ya ngome ya nyumba ya El-berithi.
sw.B: Viongozi wote wa Mnara wa Shekemu waliposikia habari hiyo, waliingia ndani ya ngome ya hekalu la El-berithi.
sw.R: Viongozi wote wa Mnara wa Shekemu walisikia yaliyotokea. Kwa hiyo waliingia katika chumba imara cha ndani cha hekalu la mungu El-berithi.

es.L: Y oyeron [esto] todos los señores de la Torre de Siquem, y entraron en la fortaleza de la casa de El-berit.
es.B: Cuando todos los líderes de la Torre de Siquem oyeron esto, entraron en la fortaleza del templo de El-berit.
es.R: Todos los líderes de la Torre de Siquem oyeron lo que había pasado. Así que entraron en la sala fuerte del interior del templo del dios El-berit.

decisions.choice: the Tower of Shechem: the fortified quarter of the city, near the temple
decisions.reason: The tower was a strong building or quarter of its own, apart from the town that Abimelech had taken. It may be the same as Beth-millo (verses 6, 20).

decisions.choice: the stronghold: an inner chamber or vault of the temple
decisions.reason: The word is rare (1 Samuel 13:6 uses it of hiding places in the hills) and its exact sense is uncertain. It seems to be a fortified inner room or cellar in the temple, where people could shut themselves in.

decisions.choice: El-berith: "God of the covenant", the god of verse 4
decisions.reason: El-berith is another name for Baal-berith, "Baal of the covenant" (verse 4; 8:33). The lords who took his silver to pay for murder now look to his house for safety.

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: the strong inner room ... the god
decisions.reason: Readable explains "stronghold" (m2) and adds "the god" as in verse 4.

source.text: וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לַאֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ כִּ֣י הִֽתְקַבְּצ֔וּ כָּֽל־בַּעֲלֵ֖י מִֽגְדַּל־שְׁכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was told to Abimelech that had gathered themselves all [the] lords of [the] Tower of Shechem.

en.L: And it was told to Abimelech that all the lords of the Tower of Shechem had gathered together.
en.B: Abimelech was told that all the leaders of the Tower of Shechem had gathered there.
en.R: Someone told Abimelech that all the leaders of the Tower of Shechem were gathered in one place.

sw.L: Naye Abimeleki akaambiwa kwamba wakuu wote wa Mnara wa Shekemu wamekusanyika pamoja.
sw.B: Abimeleki aliambiwa kwamba viongozi wote wa Mnara wa Shekemu wamekusanyika huko.
sw.R: Mtu fulani alimwambia Abimeleki kwamba viongozi wote wa Mnara wa Shekemu wamekusanyika mahali pamoja.

es.L: Y se le avisó a Abimelec que todos los señores de la Torre de Siquem se habían reunido.
es.B: A Abimelec le informaron que todos los líderes de la Torre de Siquem se habían reunido allí.
es.R: Alguien le contó a Abimelec que todos los líderes de la Torre de Siquem estaban reunidos en un solo lugar.

decisions.choice: had gathered together: all in one place
decisions.reason: The point of the report is that they are all in one place, which makes the trap that follows possible.

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַל אֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ הַר־צַלְמ֗וֹן הוּא֮ וְכָל־הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּוֹ֒ וַיִּקַּח֩ אֲבִימֶ֨לֶךְ אֶת־הַקַּרְדֻּמּ֜וֹת בְּיָד֗וֹ וַיִּכְרֹת֙ שׂוֹכַ֣ת עֵצִ֔ים וַיִּ֨שָּׂאֶ֔הָ וַיָּ֖שֶׂם עַל־שִׁכְמ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֜אמֶר אֶל־הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־עִמּ֗וֹ מָ֤ה רְאִיתֶם֙ עָשִׂ֔יתִי מַהֲר֖וּ עֲשׂ֥וּ כָמֽוֹנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up Abimelech [to] Mount Zalmon, he and all the people who [were] with him, and took Abimelech the axes in his hand and cut a branch of trees and lifted it and put [it] on his shoulder, and said to the people who [were] with him, what you have seen I have done, hurry, do like me.

en.L: And Abimelech went up Mount Zalmon, he and all the people who [were] with him, and Abimelech took the axe in his hand and cut off a branch of the trees, and he lifted it and put [it] on his shoulder, and he said to the people who [were] with him, "What you have seen me do, hurry, do as I [have done]."
en.B: Abimelech and all his troops went up Mount Zalmon. He took an axe in his hand, cut a branch from the trees, lifted it up and put it on his shoulder. Then he said to the men with him, "Quick! Do just what you have seen me do!"
en.R: Abimelech and all his men climbed Mount Zalmon. There he took an axe and cut off a branch from a tree. He lifted it onto his shoulder and told his men, "Hurry! Do what you saw me do!"

sw.L: Naye Abimeleki akapanda Mlima Salmoni, yeye na watu wote [waliokuwa] pamoja naye, naye Abimeleki akachukua shoka mkononi mwake, akakata tawi la miti, akaliinua, akaliweka begani mwake, akawaambia watu [waliokuwa] pamoja naye, "Mlichoniona nikifanya, fanyeni upesi kama mimi [nilivyofanya]."
sw.B: Abimeleki na askari wake wote walipanda Mlima Salmoni. Alichukua shoka mkononi mwake, akakata tawi la mti, akaliinua na kuliweka begani mwake. Kisha akawaambia watu waliokuwa pamoja naye, "Upesi! Fanyeni sawasawa na mlivyoniona nikifanya!"
sw.R: Abimeleki na watu wake wote walipanda Mlima Salmoni. Huko alichukua shoka akakata tawi la mti. Akaliweka begani mwake, akawaambia watu wake, "Fanyeni haraka! Fanyeni kama mlivyoniona nikifanya!"

es.L: Y subió Abimelec al monte Salmón, él y todo el pueblo que [estaba] con él, y tomó Abimelec el hacha en su mano y cortó una rama de los árboles, y la levantó y [la] puso sobre su hombro, y dijo al pueblo que [estaba] con él: «Lo que me {{plural_you:han visto|habéis visto}} hacer, {{plural_you:apresúrense|apresuraos}} [y] {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} como yo.»
es.B: Abimelec subió al monte Salmón con todas sus tropas. Tomó un hacha en la mano, cortó una rama de los árboles, la levantó y se la puso al hombro. Luego dijo a los hombres que estaban con él: «¡Rápido! ¡{{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} exactamente lo que me {{plural_you:han visto|habéis visto}} hacer!»
es.R: Abimelec y todos sus hombres subieron al monte Salmón. Allí tomó un hacha y cortó una rama de un árbol. Se la puso al hombro y les dijo a sus hombres: «¡{{plural_you:Apúrense|Daos prisa}}! ¡{{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} lo que me {{plural_you:vieron|visteis}} hacer!»

decisions.choice: Mount Zalmon: a wooded hill near Shechem
decisions.reason: The name may mean "dark" or "shady", fitting a wooded hill. It is not certain which hill it was; Mount Ebal, across the valley from Gerizim, is one suggestion.

decisions.choice: the axes in his hand: an axe, the plural form used for one tool
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the plural with "in his hand", so it is best taken as one axe (the word is plural also in 1 Samuel 13:21 and Psalm 74:5). Some think he took axes for his men as well.

decisions.choice: cutting branches from the trees: the bramble's fire of the fable
decisions.reason: In Jotham's fable the trees choose the bramble, and fire from the bramble burns them (verse 15). Now Abimelech cuts wood from the trees to burn those who made him king (verse 20).

decisions.choice: troops / men
decisions.reason: As in verse 32, "the people" with Abimelech are his fighting men: "troops" at Balanced, "men" at Readable.

decisions.choice: the axe
decisions.reason: Literal says "the axe" with the sense of m2, since "the axes in his hand" would mislead.

source.text: וַיִּכְרְת֨וּ גַם־כָּל־הָעָ֜ם אִ֣ישׁ שׂוֹכֹ֗ה וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ אַחֲרֵ֤י אֲבִימֶ֨לֶךְ֙ וַיָּשִׂ֣ימוּ עַֽל־הַצְּרִ֔יחַ וַיַּצִּ֧יתוּ עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם אֶֽת־הַצְּרִ֖יחַ בָּאֵ֑שׁ וַיָּמֻ֜תוּ גַּ֣ם כָּל־אַנְשֵׁ֧י מִֽגְדַּל־שְׁכֶ֛ם כְּאֶ֖לֶף אִ֥ישׁ וְאִשָּֽׁה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And cut also all the people, each his branch, and went after Abimelech and put [them] on the stronghold and set on fire over them the stronghold with fire, and died also all [the] men of [the] Tower of Shechem, about a thousand, man and woman.

en.L: And all the people also cut down each one his branch and followed Abimelech, and they put [them] against the stronghold and set the stronghold on fire over them, and so all the {{gender:people|men}} of the Tower of Shechem also died, about 1,000 men and women.
en.B: So all the troops also cut down a branch each and followed Abimelech. They piled the branches against the stronghold and set it on fire over the people inside. So all the {{gender:people|men}} of the Tower of Shechem died too, about 1,000 men and women.
en.R: So each of his men cut a branch and followed Abimelech. They piled the branches against the inner room and set it on fire with the people still inside. Everyone in the Tower of Shechem died, about 1,000 men and women.

sw.L: Nao watu wote pia wakakata kila mmoja tawi lake, wakamfuata Abimeleki, wakayaweka [juu ya] ngome, wakaichoma ngome moto juu yao, hata watu wote wa Mnara wa Shekemu nao wakafa, kama elfu moja, wanaume na wanawake.
sw.B: Basi askari wote nao walikata kila mmoja tawi lake, wakamfuata Abimeleki. Waliyarundika matawi kuizunguka ngome, wakaichoma moto pamoja na watu waliokuwa ndani. Basi watu wote wa Mnara wa Shekemu nao walikufa, kama elfu moja, wanaume na wanawake.
sw.R: Basi kila mmoja wa watu wake alikata tawi akamfuata Abimeleki. Waliyarundika matawi kukizunguka kile chumba cha ndani, wakakichoma moto pamoja na watu waliokuwa bado ndani. Kila mtu katika Mnara wa Shekemu alikufa, kama watu elfu moja, wanaume na wanawake.

es.L: Y todo el pueblo cortó también cada uno su rama, y siguieron a Abimelec, y [las] pusieron contra la fortaleza, y prendieron fuego a la fortaleza sobre ellos; y así murieron también todos {{gender:los habitantes|los hombres}} de la Torre de Siquem, como mil hombres y mujeres.
es.B: Así que todas las tropas cortaron también cada uno una rama y siguieron a Abimelec. Amontonaron las ramas contra la fortaleza y le prendieron fuego con la gente dentro. Así murieron también todos {{gender:los habitantes|los hombres}} de la Torre de Siquem, unos mil hombres y mujeres.
es.R: Así que cada uno de sus hombres cortó una rama y siguió a Abimelec. Amontonaron las ramas contra la sala fuerte y le prendieron fuego con la gente todavía adentro. Todos los que estaban en la Torre de Siquem murieron, unos mil hombres y mujeres.

decisions.choice: set it on fire: Jotham's curse comes true for the lords of Shechem
decisions.reason: Jotham had said, "let fire come out from Abimelech and devour the lords of Shechem and Beth-millo" (verse 20). That fire now burns them in the house of the god whose silver hired Abimelech (verse 4).

decisions.choice: all the men of the Tower: all its people, men and women
decisions.reason: The word usually means men, but the verse itself says the dead were "man and woman", so the whole population of the tower is meant. "About a thousand" is an ordinary round count.

decisions.choice: people (men)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced use the gender setting because the verse counts women among them (m2); the traditional "men" is the alternative. Readable says "everyone".

decisions.choice: the inner room
decisions.reason: Readable says "inner room" for "stronghold", as in verse 46.

source.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל־תֵּבֵ֑ץ וַיִּ֥חַן בְּתֵבֵ֖ץ וַֽיִּלְכְּדָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went Abimelech to Thebez and camped against Thebez and captured it.

en.L: And Abimelech went to Thebez and camped against Thebez and captured it.
en.B: Next Abimelech went to Thebez, laid siege to it, and captured it.
en.R: Then Abimelech went to the town of Thebez. He surrounded it with his army and captured it.

sw.L: Naye Abimeleki akaenda Thebesi, akapiga kambi dhidi ya Thebesi, akautwaa.
sw.B: Kisha Abimeleki alikwenda Thebesi, akauzingira, akauteka.
sw.R: Kisha Abimeleki alikwenda katika mji wa Thebesi. Aliuzunguka kwa jeshi lake, akauteka.

es.L: Y fue Abimelec a Tebes, y acampó contra Tebes, y la tomó.
es.B: Después Abimelec fue a Tebes, la sitió y la tomó.
es.R: Luego Abimelec fue a la ciudad de Tebes. La rodeó con su ejército y la tomó.

decisions.choice: Thebez: a town north of Shechem
decisions.reason: Thebez is probably the town of Tubas, about ten miles northeast of Shechem. The text does not say why Abimelech attacked it; most likely it too had joined the revolt.

decisions.choice: camped against: laid siege to
decisions.reason: To camp "at" or "against" a town in war means to besiege it (Joshua 10:31).

decisions.choice: the town of
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the town of" before Thebez.

source.text: וּמִגְדַּל־עֹז֮ הָיָ֣ה בְתוֹךְ־הָעִיר֒ וַיָּנֻ֨סוּ שָׁ֜מָּה כָּל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים וְהַנָּשִׁ֗ים וְכֹל֙ בַּעֲלֵ֣י הָעִ֔יר וַֽיִּסְגְּר֖וּ בַּעֲדָ֑ם וַֽיַּעֲל֖וּ עַל־גַּ֥ג הַמִּגְדָּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And a tower of strength was in [the] middle of the city, and fled there all the men and the women and all [the] lords of the city, and they shut [the door] behind them, and went up on [the] roof of the tower.

en.L: But a strong tower was in the middle of the city, and all the men and the women and all the lords of the city fled there, and they shut [the door] behind them and went up onto the roof of the tower.
en.B: But inside the city stood a strong tower, and all the men and women and all the leaders of the city fled into it. They shut themselves in and climbed up onto the roof of the tower.
en.R: But inside the city there was a strong tower. All the men and women, with all the leaders of the city, ran into it. They locked the door behind them and climbed up to the roof.

sw.L: Lakini palikuwa na mnara wenye nguvu katikati ya mji, nao wanaume wote na wanawake na wakuu wote wa mji wakakimbilia huko, wakajifungia [mlango] nyuma yao, wakapanda juu ya paa la mnara.
sw.B: Lakini ndani ya mji kulikuwa na mnara imara, nao wanaume wote na wanawake na viongozi wote wa mji walikimbilia ndani yake. Walijifungia ndani, wakapanda juu ya paa la mnara.
sw.R: Lakini ndani ya mji kulikuwa na mnara imara. Wanaume wote na wanawake, pamoja na viongozi wote wa mji, walikimbilia ndani yake. Walifunga mlango nyuma yao, wakapanda mpaka juu ya paa.

es.L: Pero había una torre fuerte en medio de la ciudad, y huyeron allí todos los hombres y las mujeres y todos los señores de la ciudad, y cerraron [la puerta] tras de sí, y subieron al techo de la torre.
es.B: Pero dentro de la ciudad había una torre fuerte, y todos los hombres y mujeres y todos los líderes de la ciudad huyeron a ella. Se encerraron y subieron al techo de la torre.
es.R: Pero dentro de la ciudad había una torre fuerte. Todos los hombres y las mujeres, con todos los líderes de la ciudad, corrieron a ella. Cerraron la puerta con llave y subieron al techo.

decisions.choice: a strong tower with a flat roof: the town's last refuge
decisions.reason: Many towns had a citadel tower inside the walls where the people could hold out when the walls fell. Its flat roof let the defenders throw down stones and other missiles on attackers below (verse 53).

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֤א אֲבִימֶ֨לֶךְ֙ עַד־הַמִּגְדָּ֔ל וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם בּ֑וֹ וַיִּגַּ֛שׁ עַד־פֶּ֥תַח הַמִּגְדָּ֖ל לְשָׂרְפ֥וֹ בָאֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Abimelech to the tower and fought against it, and drew near to [the] entrance of the tower to burn it with fire.

en.L: And Abimelech came to the tower and fought against it, and he drew near to the entrance of the tower to burn it with fire.
en.B: Abimelech came up to the tower and attacked it. He went right up to the entrance of the tower to set it on fire.
en.R: Abimelech came to the tower and attacked it. He went up close to the door to set the tower on fire.

sw.L: Naye Abimeleki akaja kwenye mnara, akapigana nao, akakaribia mlango wa mnara ili kuuchoma kwa moto.
sw.B: Abimeleki alikuja kwenye mnara akaushambulia. Alikwenda mpaka karibu kabisa na mlango wa mnara ili kuuchoma moto.
sw.R: Abimeleki alikuja kwenye mnara akaushambulia. Alikwenda karibu na mlango ili auchome mnara moto.

es.L: Y llegó Abimelec a la torre y peleó contra ella, y se acercó a la entrada de la torre para prenderle fuego.
es.B: Abimelec llegó a la torre y la atacó. Se acercó hasta la entrada de la torre para prenderle fuego.
es.R: Abimelec llegó a la torre y la atacó. Se acercó a la puerta para prenderle fuego a la torre.

decisions.choice: to burn it with fire: the same plan as at Shechem
decisions.reason: Abimelech tries again the method that destroyed the Tower of Shechem (verse 49). This time it brings him within reach of the defenders on the roof.

source.text: וַתַּשְׁלֵ֞ךְ אִשָּׁ֥ה אַחַ֛ת פֶּ֥לַח רֶ֖כֶב עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ וַתָּ֖רִץ אֶת־גֻּלְגָּלְתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And threw a woman, one, an upper millstone on [the] head of Abimelech and crushed his skull.

en.L: And a certain woman threw an upper millstone on the head of Abimelech and crushed his skull.
en.B: But a woman dropped an upper millstone on Abimelech's head and cracked his skull.
en.R: Then a woman on the roof dropped a heavy grinding stone on Abimelech's head. It broke his skull.

sw.L: Naye mwanamke mmoja akatupa jiwe la juu la kusagia juu ya kichwa cha Abimeleki, akalivunja fuvu lake.
sw.B: Lakini mwanamke mmoja aliliangusha jiwe la juu la kusagia juu ya kichwa cha Abimeleki, akalipasua fuvu lake.
sw.R: Ndipo mwanamke mmoja aliyekuwa juu ya paa aliliangusha jiwe zito la kusagia juu ya kichwa cha Abimeleki. Likavunja fuvu lake.

es.L: Y una mujer arrojó una piedra de molino de arriba sobre la cabeza de Abimelec y le rompió el cráneo.
es.B: Pero una mujer dejó caer una piedra de molino sobre la cabeza de Abimelec y le partió el cráneo.
es.R: Entonces una mujer que estaba en el techo dejó caer una pesada piedra de moler sobre la cabeza de Abimelec. Le rompió el cráneo.

decisions.choice: an upper millstone: the round stone of a hand mill
decisions.reason: Grain was ground at home between two stones; the upper one, which was moved by hand, could be carried. Grinding was women's daily work (Exodus 11:5). A woman uses an everyday tool to kill the warrior.

decisions.choice: a stone on the head of Abimelech: the end matches the crime
decisions.reason: Abimelech killed his brothers "on one stone" (verses 5, 18), and he dies by a stone. The story of his death was still told in David's day (2 Samuel 11:21).

decisions.choice: on the roof / heavy grinding stone
decisions.reason: Readable says where the woman was (verse 51) and explains "millstone".

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א מְהֵרָ֜ה אֶל־הַנַּ֣עַר׀נֹשֵׂ֣א כֵלָ֗יו וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ שְׁלֹ֤ף חַרְבְּךָ֙ וּמ֣וֹתְתֵ֔נִי פֶּן־יֹ֥אמְרוּ לִ֖י אִשָּׁ֣ה הֲרָגָ֑תְהוּ וַיִּדְקְרֵ֥הוּ נַעֲר֖וֹ וַיָּמֹֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he called quickly to the young man carrying his weapons and said to him, draw your sword and kill me, lest they say of me, a woman killed him. And pierced him his young man, and he died.

en.L: And he called quickly to the young man who carried his weapons and said to him, "Draw your sword and kill me, lest they say of me, 'A woman killed him.'" And his young man pierced him through, and he died.
en.B: He quickly called to the young man who carried his armor and said to him, "Draw your sword and kill me, so that no one can say of me, 'A woman killed him.'" So his young man ran him through, and he died.
en.R: Abimelech quickly called to the young man who carried his weapons. He said, "Take out your sword and kill me. I do not want people to say that a woman killed me." So the young man stabbed him, and Abimelech died.

sw.L: Naye akamwita upesi kijana aliyebeba silaha zake, akamwambia, "Futa upanga wako uniue, wasije wakasema habari zangu, 'Mwanamke alimwua.'" Naye kijana wake akamchoma, akafa.
sw.B: Upesi alimwita kijana aliyembebea silaha, akamwambia, "Chomoa upanga wako uniue, ili mtu yeyote asiseme habari zangu, 'Mwanamke ndiye aliyemwua.'" Basi kijana wake akamchoma, naye akafa.
sw.R: Abimeleki alimwita upesi kijana aliyembebea silaha. Akamwambia, "Chomoa upanga wako uniue. Sitaki watu waseme kwamba mwanamke aliniua." Basi kijana huyo akamchoma kwa upanga, naye Abimeleki akafa.

es.L: Y llamó apresuradamente al joven que llevaba sus armas y le dijo: «Saca tu espada y mátame, no sea que digan de mí: “Una mujer lo mató.”» Y su joven lo atravesó, y murió.
es.B: Rápidamente llamó al joven que le llevaba las armas y le dijo: «Saca tu espada y mátame, para que nadie pueda decir de mí: “Lo mató una mujer.”» Y su joven lo atravesó, y murió.
es.R: Abimelec llamó rápido al joven que le llevaba las armas. Le dijo: «Saca tu espada y mátame. No quiero que la gente diga que me mató una mujer.» Así que el joven lo atravesó con la espada, y Abimelec murió.

decisions.choice: the young man carrying his weapons: his armor-bearer
decisions.reason: A warrior's attendant carried his shield and spare weapons and fought beside him (1 Samuel 14:1; 31:4).

decisions.choice: lest they say a woman killed him: to die at a woman's hand was a disgrace for a warrior
decisions.reason: Deborah told Barak that the honor of victory would go to a woman (4:9), and Jael killed Sisera (4:21). Abimelech tries to escape that shame, but the story remembers that a woman killed him (2 Samuel 11:21).

decisions.choice: people to say that a woman killed me
decisions.reason: Readable gives the words people might say as indirect speech, to avoid a quotation inside a quotation.

source.text: וַיִּרְא֥וּ אִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כִּ֣י מֵ֣ת אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ לִמְקֹמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw [the] men of Israel that dead [was] Abimelech, and they went each to his place.

en.L: And the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, and they went each one to his place.
en.B: When the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, they all went back home.
en.R: When the Israelite soldiers saw that Abimelech was dead, they all went back home.

sw.L: Nao watu wa Israeli wakaona kwamba Abimeleki amekufa, wakaenda kila mmoja mahali pake.
sw.B: Watu wa Israeli walipoona kwamba Abimeleki amekufa, wote walirudi nyumbani.
sw.R: Askari wa Israeli walipoona kwamba Abimeleki amekufa, wote walirudi nyumbani.

es.L: Y vieron los hombres de Israel que Abimelec había muerto, y se fueron cada uno a su lugar.
es.B: Cuando los hombres de Israel vieron que Abimelec había muerto, se volvieron todos a casa.
es.R: Cuando los soldados israelitas vieron que Abimelec estaba muerto, se volvieron todos a casa.

decisions.choice: the men of Israel: the Israelite fighting men who followed Abimelech
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of Israel's army (7:23; 20:11). With their leader dead, the army breaks up and each man goes home.

decisions.choice: each to his place: they went home
decisions.reason: "To go to one's place" means to go home when a campaign or gathering ends (Numbers 24:25).

decisions.choice: soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable says "soldiers" for "men" in the sense of m1.

source.text: וַיָּ֣שֶׁב אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֵ֖ת רָעַ֣ת אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשָׂה֙ לְאָבִ֔יו לַהֲרֹ֖ג אֶת־שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶחָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And returned God [the] evil of Abimelech that he did to his father by killing his seventy brothers.

en.L: And God returned the evil of Abimelech, which he had done to his father by killing his seventy brothers.
en.B: In this way God paid Abimelech back for the evil he had done to his father by murdering his seventy brothers.
en.R: This is how God punished Abimelech for the evil thing he did to his father when he killed his seventy brothers.

sw.L: Naye Mungu akamrudishia Abimeleki uovu aliomtendea baba yake kwa kuwaua ndugu zake sabini.
sw.B: Kwa njia hii Mungu alimlipa Abimeleki kwa uovu aliomtendea baba yake kwa kuwaua ndugu zake sabini.
sw.R: Hivi ndivyo Mungu alivyomwadhibu Abimeleki kwa uovu aliomtendea baba yake alipowaua ndugu zake sabini.

es.L: Y Dios hizo volver la maldad de Abimelec, que había hecho a su padre matando a sus setenta hermanos.
es.B: Así le pagó Dios a Abimelec el mal que le había hecho a su padre al asesinar a sus setenta hermanos.
es.R: Así castigó Dios a Abimelec por el mal que le hizo a su padre cuando mató a sus setenta hermanos.

decisions.choice: God returned the evil: God made Abimelech's wrong come back on him
decisions.reason: The narrator names God as the judge behind the events of the chapter: the evil spirit he sent (verse 23), the revolt, the fire and the millstone. The word for "evil" is the one used of that spirit; the harm God sent answers the evil Abimelech had done. Wrongdoing that comes back on the doer is a theme of Israel's wisdom (Psalm 7:17; Proverbs 26:27).

decisions.choice: to his father: a crime against Jerubbaal himself
decisions.reason: Killing a man's sons wiped out his house and his name. Abimelech's crime was against the father as well as the brothers, which is why Jotham asked whether Shechem had dealt fairly with Jerubbaal (verse 16).

decisions.choice: In this way / This is how
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable link the verse to the story just told, as the Hebrew summary implies.

source.text: וְאֵ֗ת כָּל־רָעַת֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם הֵשִׁ֥יב אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּרֹאשָׁ֑ם וַתָּבֹ֣א אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם קִֽלֲלַ֖ת יוֹתָ֥ם בֶּן־יְרֻבָּֽעַל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And all [the] evil of [the] men of Shechem God returned on their head, and came to them [the] curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal.

en.L: And all the evil of the men of Shechem God returned on their heads, and the curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.
en.B: God also brought all the evil of the men of Shechem back on their own heads, and the curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.
en.R: God also punished the men of Shechem for all the evil they had done. What Jotham son of Jerubbaal said in his curse came true for them.

sw.L: Na uovu wote wa watu wa Shekemu Mungu akaurudisha juu ya vichwa vyao, nayo laana ya Yothamu mwana wa Yerubaali ikawajia.
sw.B: Mungu pia aliurudisha uovu wote wa watu wa Shekemu juu ya vichwa vyao wenyewe, nayo laana ya Yothamu mwana wa Yerubaali ikawajia.
sw.R: Mungu pia aliwaadhibu watu wa Shekemu kwa uovu wote waliokuwa wameutenda. Yale Yothamu mwana wa Yerubaali aliyosema katika laana yake yaliwapata.

es.L: Y toda la maldad de los hombres de Siquem la hizo Dios volver sobre sus cabezas, y vino sobre ellos la maldición de Jotam hijo de Jerobaal.
es.B: Dios también hizo recaer sobre sus propias cabezas toda la maldad de los hombres de Siquem, y vino sobre ellos la maldición de Jotam hijo de Jerobaal.
es.R: Dios también castigó a los hombres de Siquem por todo el mal que habían hecho. Lo que Jotam hijo de Jerobaal dijo en su maldición se cumplió en ellos.

decisions.choice: returned on their head: made their wrong fall on themselves
decisions.reason: To bring something "on someone's head" is to make him bear the consequences of what he has done (1 Kings 2:32-33; Psalm 7:17).

decisions.choice: the curse of Jotham: his words in verse 20 fulfilled
decisions.reason: Jotham had called down fire on both Abimelech and the lords of Shechem (verse 20). Both have now been destroyed, each by the other, as he said.

decisions.choice: God brought it about: the curse came true because God judged
decisions.reason: The verse sets God's repaying and Jotham's curse side by side. The curse had power not of itself but because God, whom Jotham asked to listen (verse 7), judged the wrong done to Jerubbaal's house.

decisions.choice: punished
decisions.reason: Readable says "punished" for the picture of returning evil on their heads (m1).
